### 47.4 Reading

* **The year factor is now a published number with its page on every row**, and the
  assumption and the flag are gone from both studies. The factor the placeholder had guessed
  (1.15) was 7 % low against the index's own 1.233; section 45's honest 1.0000 was 19 % low.
* **The shares do not move** (the factor multiplies every itemized row and the square-foot
  RCN alike): bucket errors and the row-share distance are unchanged to within 0.05 points,
  and the photo-visible and kind C scores are identical. The regression check holds.
* **The reconciliation halves its gap and still does not reconcile.** With the dollars
  escalated to 2024 the replacement cost new is 9-10 % above the basis and the depreciated
  total 13-14 % below it, outside the 10 % tolerance, so the allocation stays withheld and the
  diagnosis stands: the implied uniform factor moved from 1.13 (the schedule short of the
  basis) to 0.91 (the schedule, depreciated at the appraiser's 21 % physical rate, short by the
  depreciation itself). The remaining gap is not the index: it is the depreciation rate and the
  5-year side (section 44.4's cabinets, FF&E and window treatments), which the engineer's
  report allocates without depreciating. That is a structure-model question for the next
  section, not a cost-index one; the index did what it could, and the result now says so with
  `cost_index.status: published` instead of a `missing` note.
* **What the firm does now**: nothing in code. On the deployment, `python -m
  basis.costs.refresh seed` once, then either `COST_INDEX_FETCH=on` and the monthly job, or
  `POST /v1/cost-indices` with the year's value and its citation. The 2024 study reruns its
  assets step and prices on 1.2330 with the page cited.

### 47.5 Tests and gates

Unit: `tests/unit/costs/` (the book fetcher, the public page parser against a recorded copy of
the 2024 page with the 2026 page's comment decoy, the selection and its priority, the CLI
parser and the export round trip; 25 tests), the domain tests updated for the store-first
lookup, the result's `cost_index`, the metadata of the two tables. Integration with Docker:
`tests/integration/db/test_cost_index_store.py` (append-only, versioned, never twice; the
refresh job seeds once and adds nothing twice, skips a network source while fetching is off
with the reason, asks once when on, records a failure without writing; the manual path; 11
tests), `tests/api/test_cost_indices.py` (owner-only entry, validation, 409 on a repeat with
nothing written, revision, listing, ledger, idempotency; 15 tests), migration 0016 forward and
back, the OpenAPI contract on the new routes, and the lifecycle study whose 2024 index now
arrives through the store's manual path. Gates from `backEnd/`: `ruff check`, `ruff format
--check`, `mypy basis evals` clean; unit `-m "not integration and not slow"` and the
integration set: see the PR for the tallies. Client data: none in the repository (the recorded
page is a public marketing page's index block; `tooling/check_no_client_data.py` clean).

## 48. Rooms open named, typed and floored: the name's words first, then every photo's vote (2026-10-30)

The live runs of section 38 opened the Rooms review on the per-photo grouping: 49 rooms for
52 photos, every name carrying its floor ("2nd Floor Bed 2"), and some rooms typed
`ambiguous` or wrong although their file names said what they were; the engineer fixed two
room types by hand besides the 16 merges. Since PR #93 the room type also picks
classification variants and is part of the firm conventions' key, so a wrong type now moves
buckets, not only the review screen. This section makes a room's three fields independent and
measures them on the client property's 52 photos, before and after, without a paid run.
Section 47 is PR #97's. No client name, address or amount appears here; room descriptions
are generic.

### 48.1 What the Rooms review showed, and why (verified in code and data)

Read from the local stack's database (revision 1 of the four live studies of 2026-10-29/30,
read-only) and the stored per-photo run `vision_decomposed_v2_gpt61sol` (3 repeats):

* **Names kept the floor.** The room's name was the file name's remainder (`display_name`),
  floor prefix included, though the floor already had its own column: 36 of the 49 rooms.
* **The type was the model's alone.** A file-name room's type was the per-photo model's
  majority (`_vote_room_type` at creation, `vote_identity` in `reconcile_rooms`' vote); the
  file name was read for the room key and the floor, never for the type. A one-photo room whose
  photo answered `ambiguous` therefore opened as Ambiguous: the stored run answered `ambiguous`
  11 times in 156 (a mechanical room named after its equipment, a bedroom's seating area, the
  three basement bedrooms), and the live studies 1 to 2 rooms each. Wrong confident answers
  went through the same way (basement bedrooms as `storage` or `basement`, a bedroom's seating
  area as `living_room`, an entrance as `lobby`): 4 to 7 rooms per repeat with a wrong or
  ambiguous type.
* **A photo with no component never voted.** Its answer existed only in its `components`
  rows' `raw` (`_answer` in `reconcile_rooms`); 3 of the stored run's 156 answers listed no
  component. Such a room kept the answer of whichever photo was analyzed first.
* **`ROOM_RECONCILE=false` skipped the vote** (the activity returned before planning), so
  those rooms kept the first photo's answer too.
* **Exterior views took the model's floor**: 0 to 3 of the 13 site views per live study were
  `floor 1` (5 in the four studies).
* Photos left without a room: none with descriptive file names (every name is a room hint);
  with camera names the model's identity groups and an `ambiguous` answer goes to the
  Unassigned room (1 to 4 photos of 52).

### 48.2 The standard

The RESO Data Dictionary 2.0 keeps a listing's `RoomType` (33 values, the ordinal inside the
value: "Bedroom 2", "Bathroom 1") and `RoomLevel` (Basement, First, Second, Third, and the
relative Main, Lower, Upper) as separate fields (dd.reso.org/DD2.0/lookups/RoomType,
/RoomLevel, read 2026-10-30). Basis's `rooms` already had the three columns; what was missing
was filling them from the right evidence each. The relative levels have no number, so they
are not read: an unknown floor stays null.

### 48.3 What changed (`basis.vision.rooms`, `reconcile_rooms`, migration 0017)

* `room_name`: the file name without the floor prefix the labelling rule identified
  (`<n>st/nd/rd/th Floor`, `Basement`), ordinal and words kept: "2nd Floor Bedroom 2" is
  `Bedroom 2` on floor `2`, "Basement Bath" `Bath` on `0`. A name with no identified floor is
  unchanged, and so is a name that is only a floor ("Basement").
* `name_room_type`: the type the name says, from a fixed vocabulary of common US residential
  and small-commercial room terms (the RESO lookup's among them), longest phrase first, words
  after a locator ("to", "from", "off", ...) ignored, the last match winning (the head of an
  English noun phrase is last: "Bed 2 Bath" is a bathroom, "Bed 3 Seating Area" a bedroom).
  A name with no room word ("Extra Area Seating Area", "Access from 1st Floor") says nothing.
* `resolve_room`, one function for creation, the vote, `group_photos` and the eval: type =
  the name's, else the per-photo answers' majority (`ambiguous` abstains); floor = a file name's,
  else none for exterior and parking (a floor does not apply to the grounds), else the answers'
  most common, else null; `0` is kept as the basement. The name is never voted.
* `photo_room_answers` (migration 0017): `analyze_photo` records each analysis' room type,
  confidence, floor and ordinal, so every analyzed photo votes, components or not; a photo
  carried into a revision answers from its latest analysis. Photos analyzed before the
  migration vote from their component rows as before (no backfill).
* The vote runs with the room step off too, and every change is a `room.voted` event (actor
  `model`, before/after, the source of each field: `file_name`, `model` or `none`;
  docs/api/TIMELINE_AND_AUDIT.md).
* Unchanged on purpose: room keys (`group_key`), aliases, assignments and the merge path; a
  room a reviewer corrected (`source = manual`) is never voted and no room is ever renamed, so
  rooms grouped before this change keep their names; rooms are never merged because names or
  types match (two "Bath" rooms on floors 1 and 0 stay two rooms).
* Found while testing the round trip: a `room` correction with a numeric `floor` (`0`) passed
  `POST /decisions` and then failed `apply_corrections` on the database write (asyncpg
  `DataError`), so the rejection would never apply. Now a whole number is stored as its text,
  and a value the activity cannot store (empty name, `true`, `2.5`, out of range) is a 422 at
  the route (`BASIS-CORRECT-027` in the activity).
* The export's assets CSV gains a last column `room_floor`, since two rooms may now share a
  name.

### 48.4 Measured: the 52 photos, no model call (`evals.room_metadata`)

The grouping scored is `initial_rooms`, the function the activities' writes equal (an
integration test compares the database after `assign_room_by_name`, the answer rows and the
vote with it). "Before" is main `7aa78c3`'s production path replayed by a scratch script
(creation by the first photo in file order, then `vote_room` on the photos with component
rows). Truth: the room labels (`room_inventory_v1.json`, 33 rooms; for a view the labels alias
into another room, its photos' labels), with `entry` as hallway and `stairs` as stairway. The
name is scored against the engineer's own words without the leading floor, which checks the
format, not a model. Ranges are over repeats.

**How to read this table.** Does reading the room's name first give rooms the right name, type and floor?

- **Models**: the exact model id, its provider, the reasoning effort and the temperature as sent. "temperature default" means the model takes no temperature (reasoning models), so the provider's default applies.
- **Rooms grouped by**: File names: 49 rooms from photo file names. With the 16 aliases: merged into the engineer's 33 rooms. Camera names: rooms from the AI's guess.
- **Rule**: Before: the old rule (the AI's vote only). After: the room name's words first, then the photos' vote.
- **Rooms**: Rooms produced (ranges are over studies or repeats).
- **Name right** (higher is better): Rooms whose name matches the engineer's words.
- **Room type right** (higher is better): Rooms with the right room type.
- **Floor right** (higher is better): Rooms with the right floor.
- **All three right** (higher is better): Rooms with name, type and floor all right.
- **Rooms typed 'ambiguous'** (lower is better): Rooms left with no clear type.
- **Photos with no room** (lower is better): Photos left in the Unassigned room.
- **Tokens (input / output)**: Tokens the run used: input (what the model read) / output (what it wrote; "thinking" is the part spent reasoning, billed as output). "Not recorded" means the run kept no token counts; nothing is estimated.

Per photo (the type of the room each photo is in against its own label), file names: 45–48
of 52 before, 51–52 after. All three fields right over every room and repeat: 46 of 196 → 194
of 196 (live), 39 of 147 → 147 of 147 (stored run). The three misses left are model-only
fields (the name says nothing, or no file name gives a floor): a seating area typed `hallway`
in one live study (labelled living room), and the mechanical room given floor `0` by the model
in one live study, where the room label has no floor but its photos are labelled basement.
The room count does not change (49, or 33 after the merges): proposing the merges is not this
change. The camera-name rows do not change either: the model-identity path was left as it was.

**What the number does not prove.** The vocabulary was written knowing these 52 names, so the
file-name rows are a regression, not out-of-sample evidence; the 30 other names in the tests
(listing and inspection terms) were written with it too. A second client package is the test.

### 48.5 Not done, and what it touches

* **Downstream not replayed**: the voted type is the room step's input (its path and prompt)
  and the classifier's context, so rooms whose type changed here (the basement bedrooms, the
  mechanical room, a seating area, an entrance) will get different room-step and convention
  keys; neither was rerun (both are paid or need a live study).
* **Not delivered: "every photo must be in a room before Rooms approval."** This change does
  not add that guard; it depends on integrating the separate, uncommitted room-management work
  (its hand-over note `ROOM_MANAGEMENT_HANDOFF.md`), which implements it at `POST /decisions`,
  and that integration is Bryan's decision. Until then a Rooms review can still be approved
  with photos unplaced. Where this change decides whether a photo is placed (`initial_rooms`,
  `evals.room_metadata`) it uses that work's rule: no assignment, or the room named exactly
  `Unassigned`.
* Floors written as words ("Second Floor", "Floor 2", "Ground Floor") are not read, so such
  a name keeps its words and the floor comes from the photos or stays null; the room key rule
  is the labeller's and was not changed.
* The model-identity path (camera names) still takes the model's floor for exterior views.
* Rooms grouped before this change keep the floor in their names until regrouped.

### 48.6 Tests and gates

`tests/unit/vision/test_room_metadata.py` (names, the vocabulary on the package's and 30 other
names, sources per field, basement `0`, unknown floors, the grounds, the vote with

analyses, camera names and the Unassigned tray, corrected-floor parsing);
`tests/unit/activities/test_reconcile_rooms.py` (the answer row, the `room.voted` event and
its retry, a carried photo's answer, a reviewer's rename, refloor and move surviving the vote,
a re-analysis and a retry across the two gates, the vote with the room step off, legacy names
and legacy rows); `tests/api/test_room_metadata_api.py` (`GET /rooms` → `POST /decisions` →
`apply_corrections` → the vote → `GET /rooms` at the next revision with provenance; the 422s;
the database equal to `initial_rooms`); `tests/unit/evals/test_room_metadata.py`. Gates: see
the PR.
## 49. The reconciliation gap closed for documented reasons: the house's baths and heating, the residual added back, one cost basis (2026-10-31)

Question (section 47.4): with every cost factor a cited RSMeans index, both live exports of the
client property replay to RCNLD 14.2 % (run 3A) and 13.4 % (run 3B) below the purchase price
less land, outside the 10 % tolerance, so the allocation is withheld. The guide does not allow
scaling the schedule to the basis (ATG ch. 3 D(3)-(5)); it asks for "an analysis of the
available data and methodology ... to assess and determine the source of the difference"
among five causes (D(6)). Which part of the gap does each cause explain, what does the guide
or the cost source say to do about it, and does the schedule reconcile once those things are
done? Section 48 is PR #99's. Design: STRUCTURE_MODEL.md sections 8 (the decomposition,
written before any code changed) and 9 (what was built and measured). No paid run; no client
dollar amount here (shares and points; artifacts, private:
`work/e2e_artifacts/reconciliation_gap_2026-10-31/`).

### 49.1 The decomposition

Against the engineer's report (implied RCN per row, section 34) our RCN is 0.775 of the
engineer's: thin in MEP (0.59), interior construction (0.62), the 5-year equipment and finishes
(0.38, 0.73) and the land improvements we cannot measure (0.13); the engineer's RCN is itself
12 % above the appraiser's cost new plus site improvements and is written down by one factor
(0.710) on every row, so it says where our RCN is thin, not what it should be. By the guide's
five causes (STRUCTURE_MODEL.md 8.2):

| Cause (ATG D(6)) | Finding | Points of B, 3A / 3B (estimated before coding; measured) |
|---|---|---|
| Land FMV | B equals the engineer's (12 % flat); the appraisal's site value would move it 0.6 % | not a cause here |
| Components and quantities not identified | The square-foot model was priced as RSMeans' base house (one full and one half bath, forced air: step 1 of the book's three); the house has six full baths and hot-water heat, which the facing page prices as modifications and alternatives (step 2: "Add or subtract the modifications, adjustments, and alternatives") | 7.8 / 7.8; measured 7.8 / 7.8 |
| | The Specialties residual (custom cabinets, countertops, sink, water heater less the itemized ones) was reported but left out of the RCN total; C.4(1)-(2): a residual is assigned to the building and added back to reconcile | 3.7 / 3.5; measured 3.7 / 3.4 |
| | Fire alarm, data cabling and locksets were priced on top of the components that include them (section 3.6 says carved): a double count | -0.5 / -0.7; measured -0.5 / -0.6 |
| | Evidenced site and furnishing assets without a quantity (the driveway alone is 6.4 % of B in the engineer's RCN) | not closable without a measurement |
| Cost estimates and factors | Itemized rows at RSMeans bare cost while the square-foot components carry the installing contractor's O&P ("The costs in components 1 through 9 include overhead and profit for the installing contractor", PDF p.21) | 1.2 / 1.3; measured 1.2 / 1.2 |
| Depreciation factors | The appraiser's 21.4 % equals the age-life 15 / 70; per-class rates need the items' ages, and the building's effective age on shorter lives would only widen the gap | none |
| Indirect costs | The model's general contractor's O&P (item 10) spread over the components but subtracted without it: the concealed 39-year rows carried the 5-year rows' share (C.11(2): pro rata) | 0 on the total; dollars move to the itemized rows |

### 49.2 What was built

The four changes are settings, each measured alone: `STRUCTURE_MODIFICATIONS` (the 18 facing
pages' bath modifications and heating and cooling alternatives, re-read as images; the bath's
plumbing to Mechanical by the three-fixture assembly over the Average full bath, 61.9 %, its
finishes to Interiors; heating and cooling to HVAC), `STRUCTURE_SPECIALTIES_RESIDUAL` (the
residual written as `specialties_residual`, a building row, contested, cited to ATG ch. 3
C.4(1) p.31: rules row 68, `RULES_VERSION` 2026-10-31.1), `COST_BASIS` (the line's Total Incl
O&P; a row without the column, the six legacy rows, by the book's markups: material + 10 %,
labor + 72 %, equipment + 10 %, which reproduce the printed column within 5 % on 64 of the
private table's 67 rows), `STRUCTURE_OVERHEAD_ALLOCATION` (the model's item 10 over components
1-9 on every row inside the model, none outside it: C.11(2)-(3)). The small systems are carved
(a defect against section 3.6, fixed without a setting). Defaults are all four on. Response
shapes are additive: one more concealed row, new keys in `building_rcn.inputs`, the cost
basis and markup written into each cost row's `source_row`, the causes' text; the result's
`not_produced` never lists the residual. `evals.reprice_export` gains `--cost-basis` and
`--overhead`, `evals.structure_replay` the new axes, and `evals.gap_sweep` runs them.

### 49.3 The sweep

Each export repriced three ways (bare; installed; installed with the general contractor's
O&P) and replayed twelve ways (square-foot model with and without the modifications, the
appraisal's cost new; the residual reported or written; the small systems added or carved):
36 cells per export, every one scored by the e2e scorer with the July 2024 index (section 47),
cost $0, about 10 ms a cell. Each step added in turn:

**How to read this table.** Which documented corrections close the gap between our cost and the purchase price?

- **Models**: the exact model id, its provider, the reasoning effort and the temperature as sent. "temperature default" means the model takes no temperature (reasoning models), so the provider's default applies.
- **Study A: gap to the price (%) / balances?**: Whether the depreciated cost lands within 10 % of the purchase price less land ('reconciled'), and how far below it, in percent (negative = above).
- **Study A: share of dollars by class: 5 / 7 / 15 / 39 years (%)**: How the dollars split across the 5, 7, 15 and 39-year classes; the engineer's is 14.4 / 0.4 / 5.1 / 80.2.
- **Study A: class share error, average / worst (points)** (lower is better): Average and worst gap, in percentage points, between our dollar share and the engineer's across the 5, 7, 15 and 39-year classes.
- **Study A: row-share distance (points)** (lower is better): How far our dollar shares per engineer report line are from the engineer's, in points (total variation distance; 0 = identical).
- **Study B: gap to the price (%) / balances?**: Whether the depreciated cost lands within 10 % of the purchase price less land ('reconciled'), and how far below it, in percent (negative = above).
- **Study B: share of dollars by class: 5 / 7 / 15 / 39 years (%)**: How the dollars split across the 5, 7, 15 and 39-year classes; the engineer's is 14.4 / 0.4 / 5.1 / 80.2.
- **Study B: class share error, average / worst (points)** (lower is better): Average and worst gap, in percentage points, between our dollar share and the engineer's across the 5, 7, 15 and 39-year classes.
- **Study B: row-share distance (points)** (lower is better): How far our dollar shares per engineer report line are from the engineer's, in points (total variation distance; 0 = identical).
- **Tokens (input / output)**: Tokens the run used: input (what the model read) / output (what it wrote; "thinking" is the part spent reasoning, billed as output). "Not recorded" means the run kept no token counts; nothing is estimated.

Engineer: 14.4 / 0.4 / 5.1 / 80.2. Gap is B less RCNLD over B. Kind C rows: 8 produced, 7 in
the engineer's bucket in every cell (Access Control, section 44). Regression line: the
photo-visible rows are 35 evidenced / 35 bucket right (3A) and 35 / 34 (3B) in all 72 cells.
With the production cell the allocation is no longer withheld: factor 1.022 (3A) and 1.017
(3B) on RCNLD.

**The pick.** Production: the square-foot model with all four changes. The sweep's
bucket-error ranking (cells that reconcile on both exports) puts two cells first that skip the
modifications (1.26 against 1.44 points mean, at a 9.5 % gap against 1.8 %): they price a
six-bath, hot-water house as the book's base house, step 2 of the book's method left out,
which is a defect kept rather than an alternative, and they are set aside as section 44 set
aside the unsourced cells. Among the cells that apply every change, the square-foot model
leads the appraisal's cost new (1.44 against 1.74 points; gaps 1.8 % and 1.9 %), so
`STRUCTURE_RCN_SOURCE` keeps its default and its runner-up.

### 49.4 Reading

1. **The gap was the method, not the index or the depreciation.** Four sourced corrections,
   each estimated before any code and each measured to within 0.1 point of its estimate, take
   RCNLD from 14.2 % and 13.4 % below the basis to 2.0 % and 1.6 %: the RSMeans square-foot
   method applied in full (7.8 points), the residual added back as the guide's residual
   approach says (3.5-3.7), one cost basis for the itemized rows and the model (1.2), less the
   double count the design doc had already ruled out (0.5-0.6). The depreciation rate and the
   land were not touched, and nothing is scaled.
2. **The 5-year side moved toward the engineer.** Once the itemized rows carry the installing
   contractor's O&P and their share of the general contractor's, the 5-year share rises from
   11.3 to 14.1 % on 3A (engineer 14.4 %) and 8.4 to 10.4 % on 3B; the bucket error falls from
   2.06 to 0.55 points on 3A and 3.49 to 2.34 on 3B. On 3A, the study the engineer corrected at
   every gate, every bucket is within 0.8 points of the engineer's.
3. **A correct building addition can worsen the share score.** The modifications raise the
   building's share past the engineer's (85.2 % on 3A before the pricing changes) because the 5-
   and 15-year sides still lack what nobody measured (the driveway, walks and fences, the FF&E
   without a cost row). In dollars the building moves toward the engineer's; the share metric
   cannot tell the two apart, which is why the pick is not the metric's first row (49.3).
4. **What got worse, reported rather than tuned.** The row-share distance rises 2.0 points on
   3A and 0.7 on 3B: Interior Framing / Partitions falls to 7.2 % of the schedule (engineer
   12.7 %: the itemized interiors now carry their general contractor's O&P instead of the
   partition residual) and Plumbing rises to 7.7 % (engineer 5.2 %: the added baths' plumbing
   at one national ratio), while the façade and framing rows move toward the engineer's.
5. **What remains open.** The unmeasured site assets (a takeoff from the site plan or a
   measurement at intake), per-class depreciation (the items' ages), permits and fees beyond
   the model's "design" (no source in the corpus), the bath split's single ratio, and the
   "Not Heated" alternative (its sign misprinted on the custom and luxury pages, not used).
   One property decides this; `evals.gap_sweep` reruns on any export in seconds.

### 49.5 Tests and gates

`tests/unit/domain/test_structure.py` (all 18 models carry their page's modifications and one
page's values as read; the UAD bath count and the ".5" decimal; heating and cooling to the
page's alternative; the modifications in the building RCN, a deducted half bath, cooling in
the ductwork the heating has, none on the appraisal's figure; `split_building` foots and puts
each addition in its component; the Mechanical residual gives each addition to its row and
keeps the ratio when a negative addition is too large; the small systems carved and the
laterals not; the overhead markup per model and `inside_model`; a written residual is not an
unassigned remainder; the causes say how rows were priced; the residual written and reported),
`tests/unit/domain/test_cost_table.py` (Total Incl O&P, the conversion for a row without it
and for the legacy rows, the markup recorded; the bare-basis tests pinned explicitly),
`tests/unit/domain/test_rules_table.py` (the new row, contested, building, the version),
`tests/unit/evidence/test_result.py` (the residual is never `not_produced`),
`tests/unit/activities/test_process_assets.py` (a row inside the model carries the general
contractor's O&P and an appliance does not, the residual row written, the four settings
restore the behaviour before), `tests/lifecycle/test_intake_takeoff.py` (the fabricated house
reconciles at a re-tuned price, as section 44 tuned it), and the counts of concealed rows (13
to 14) across the API, export, lifecycle and failure tests. `tests/LEDGER.md` has each. Gates
from `backEnd/`: see the PR for the tallies.

## 50. Live run 4 on main, and a release no longer hides the firm's rulings (2026-10-31)

Question: does main (9c430aa, PRs #92-#101) produce a reconciled, correctly bucketed study live,
on the stack as deployed? One study of the client property, every gate approved as the model
left it, on a stack rebuilt from main with migrations to 0018, the worker started before the
API, and the cost index store seeded (2024 HCI 294.8, factor 1.2330). Artifacts, private:
`work/e2e_artifacts/live_2026-10-31_run4/`; dollars in `reports/E2E_LIVE_RUN4_2026-10-31.md`.

### 50.1 What the live run measured

It completed in 11.4 minutes with no failed stage and no retry. Reconciliation passed: RCNLD
is 1.0 % under the purchase price less land. The allocation was produced and sums to the basis
to the cent. The structure model produced 8 of 8 concealed rows, 7 in the right bucket (Access
Control is y5 against the engineer's y39, contested, section 44). Rooms (#99): 49 of 49 named
and typed, 36 of 49 with a floor; the 13 without are 12 exterior rooms and 1 mechanical room.
Cost trail (#101): 384 of 384 assets carry a recorded trail.

Bucket right: 27 of 35 evidenced rows, against 34-35 of 35 in run 3. The max bucket share error
is 6.9 points. The eight wrong rows are Moldings, Fireplaces, Raised Wood Paneling, Wood
Flooring, Wall Coverings, Interior Half Walls, Kitchen/Utility/Laundry Sink, and
Security/Exterior Lighting.

### 50.2 Why: the rules version hid every ruling

The firm's conventions were keyed by `RULES_VERSION`, and the reader served only the running
version. #94 and #100 moved the version from `2026-10-29.1` to `2026-10-31.1` by adding rows
only: the diff is 222 insertions and one deletion, the version string. All 157 stored rulings
(233 approvals) were hidden. They include baseboard, hardwood floor, wainscoting, half wall,
fireplace and sink at 5 years, which are the rows run 4 lost.

### 50.3 The fix

CLASSIFICATION_CONVENTIONS.md section 10 has the design.

* A convention's key now ends in the fingerprint of the rules-table row its label resolves
  to, not in the release name. A ruling is retired when its row, a variant or the path to it
  changes, and only then. The row's explanation (category, note, citations) is not part of the
  fingerprint, so a re-citation pass retires nothing.
* Migration 0019 re-keys stored rows to the fingerprint of the released table they were made
  under. It carries those tables frozen from git (`evals.freeze_rule_fingerprints`).

Checked:

* No row changed across the three releases: each 10-29.1 and 10-30.1 row has the same digest
  in 10-31.1, and the frozen 10-31.1 table equals the running one.
* Mutants of the merge, of the conflict rule, of the version filter and of the downgrade's
  keeper all fail the migration test.
* Removing the reader's fingerprint filter, or keying by the release again, fails the
  repository tests.

### 50.4 Measured on a copy of the stack's database

The migration ran on two copies, never on the live database.

| copy | stored rows | re-keyed | merged | kept at old key, not served | current under the running code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rulings as they stood before run 4 | 157 | 157 (233 approvals) | 0 | 0 | 157 |
| full database | 252 | 169 (300 approvals) | 68 | 15 (28 approvals) | 169 |

On the full copy, 15 contexts take run 4's answer because its blanket approval is the latest
ruling. A live `put` settles a disagreement the same way.

Replay of run 4's export with the migrated rows (`evals.conventions_replay`, policy `tiered`,
keys kept as stored, so only current fingerprints serve):

| | bucket right | max bucket share error | bucket shares y5 / y7 / y15 / y39 |
|---|---|---|---|
| live run 4 | 27 / 35 | 6.9 points | 7.5 / 0.9 / 4.5 / 87.1 |
| with the fix, rulings before run 4 | 34 / 35 | 2.2 points | 12.3 / 0.9 / 4.3 / 82.5 |
| with the fix, full copy | 31 / 35 | 4.9 points | 9.6 / 0.9 / 4.3 / 85.2 |
| engineer | | | 14.4 / 0.4 / 5.1 / 80.2 |

The remaining wrong row is Fireplaces, as in run 3B: fireplace has no rules row, and the
firm's rulings on it disagree (y5 and y39 rows in the same rooms, keyed by different materials).

### 50.5 Also found

* `python -m basis.costs.refresh` with no subcommand, the documented monthly job, raised
  `AttributeError`. It is fixed on its own branch, `claude/refresh-cli-default`.
* The store starts empty on a new database, so a deployment must seed it once.
* A study run 4 approved without corrections promotes the pipeline's answers as the firm's
  rulings. On a shared environment, a test study is approved only by someone who reviewed it.

## 51. The study report and the preparer's schedule (2026-10-31)

Question: can Basis hand over the deliverable, a report an engineer signs and a schedule a
preparer imports, with every figure traceable to the approved export and every total tied?
Design, decisions and as-built: STUDY_REPORT_SPEC.md section 11. API: docs/api/REPORT.md.
No paid run.

### 51.1 What the standard asks

The ATG's chapter 4 lists thirteen quality elements (C.1-C.13) and nine report elements
(D.1-D.9), with no prescribed format. ASCSP's standards are members-only and aligned with
the ATG.

Three public sample reports were read:

* an engineered study, 34 pages;
* an automated single-family study, 247 pages;
* a duplex study, 75 pages, built with ReportLab.

None maps its pages to the ATG elements. The automated sample applies 100 % bonus to a
property its own settlement statement dates to June 2024. The rate keys on the acquisition
date (P.L. 119-21), so Basis's schedule carries the acquisition date separately and the
synthetic test reproduces that case: 40 %.

### 51.2 Renderer

Run 4's real content went through Typst 0.15 and WeasyPrint 70: 384 items, 47 photographs
with 328 outlined objects. Both were byte-identical across processes on one machine. Only
Typst was byte-identical between the Mac and the Linux worker image (Pango differs), and it
was ten times faster. Typst was chosen (STUDY_REPORT_SPEC 11.8.1).

### 51.3 Run 4, through the report (private copy)

* **Lines:** 263. Quantities measured once for the whole property folded into one line
  each; there were 295 before folding, 32 of them zero-valued copies.
* **Awaiting a measurement:** 89 items, outside the totals.
* **Categories:** 67, from 186 free-text names in the export.
* **Ties:** classes, categories, schedule rows and price plus costs less land all tie to the
  depreciable basis to the cent.
* **Bonus default:** acquired and placed in service in 2024, so 60 %.
* **Speed and size:** 52 photographs composed in 1.0 s; the PDF rendered in 0.2 s, 45
  pages, 3.7 MB.
* **Byte-identical:** the PDF, the CSV and the XLSX on a second build.
* **Flags in the limiting conditions:**
  * the land method: the appraisal's site value was available but the flat percentage was used;
  * the uniform depreciation.

### 51.4 Checks

* `tests/unit/report/` (54): the tax terms and the bonus boundaries; ties and refusals
  (each `BASIS-REPORT` code); folding and nomenclature; the schedule's limits and stability;
  every figure present in the PDF text; site visits stated only when made; Exhibit A edges at
  exact pixel positions.
* `tests/api/test_study_report.py` (3).
* The lifecycle assertions in `test_intake_takeoff.py`: the PDF and schedule written and tied
  to the allocation, the unpriced systems disclosed. In `test_happy_path.py`, a study without
  an intake records the skip, BASIS-REPORT-002.

### 51.5 Not yet

* Storing the report inputs (the firm's profile, the study's answers) and signing in Basis:
  every report is a DRAFT until then.
* Vendor import layouts: they wait for a preparer's template.
* A side-by-side review of the PDF with the design partner.

## 52. Signing the report in Basis (2026-10-31)

**Question.** Can an engineer turn the section 51 DRAFT into a final, signed report inside Basis? The
signature must be defensible as an electronic signature, and the engineer must sign exactly the report
they reviewed.

**Design.** Laid out in STUDY_REPORT_SPEC 11.13:
- Inputs: a firm profile (owners), study answers (engineers) and a signature row per revision
  (migration 0020).
- The signature maps to the four elements ESIGN and UETA practice asks for: intent, attribution,
  association with the record, and retention.
- The engineer signs the preview they opened. Rendering is deterministic, so the API re-renders the
  preview and compares its sha256 with the one the engineer reviewed.

**Results.**
- **Tests:**
  - API: 4 tests. Five mutants of the checks each fail them.
  - Migration 0020: 1 test.
  - Unit: 2 tests.
  - Web: 7 node tests.
  - The rows are in `tests/LEDGER.md`.
- **Run 4, on a copy of the dev database:**
  - The preview took 0.8 to 1.0 s for 45 pages and 3.7 MB, and was byte-identical twice.
  - Changing an input after the preview refused the signature (412 BASIS-REPORT-010).
  - The signed PDF carries the signature block and no DRAFT mark.
  - The `report.signed` event is in the timeline.

**What it is not.**
- It is not a PAdES certificate signature.
- It is not a PE seal. State engineering boards govern seals. We found no source that requires a seal
  on a cost segregation report.

**Open.**
- Interviews and prior depreciation (look-back studies) can be set through the API, but the app has
  no form for them yet.
- The design's PDF viewer labels the preview "Local PDF · not uploaded".

## 54. A decision outranks a model answer: the Fireplaces row (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Run 5 (section 53) got 34 of 35 rows right; the engineer had ruled on the one wrong
row, Fireplaces. Why did the ruling not serve, and what rule fixes it without losing the cost
savings?

**Finding.** Study 3B, a plain run approved by the driver without a correction, had promoted the
model's 39-year fireplace (material not read) as an approved model answer at the exact key, with
two approvals. The engineer's 5-year rulings carry a material, one tier down. An exact match
consults no coarser tier, and at tiers 2 and 3 approvals alone settle a disagreement, so a blanket
approval outvoted a correction. CLASSIFICATION_CONVENTIONS.md section 11 has the rule.

**Replays of run 5's export** (no paid run), the production router each time:

**How to read this table.** Which rule for reusing the firm's rulings keeps the engineer's decisions on top?

- **Models**: the exact model id, its provider, the reasoning effort and the temperature as sent. "temperature default" means the model takes no temperature (reasoning models), so the provider's default applies.
- **Assets classified from rulings** (higher is better): Assets of run 5's 384 classified from the firm's stored rulings instead of the AI.
- **Report lines in the right tax class (of 35)** (higher is better): Of the 35 engineer report lines found, how many land in the engineer's tax class.
- **Worst class share error** (lower is better): Largest gap, in percentage points, between our share of dollars and the engineer's in any tax class.
- **Tokens (input / output)**: Tokens the run used: input (what the model read) / output (what it wrote; "thinking" is the part spent reasoning, billed as output). "Not recorded" means the run kept no token counts; nothing is estimated.

| Which stored rulings are reused, and in what order | Models (provider, effort, temperature) | Assets classified from rulings ↑ | Report lines in the right tax class (of 35) ↑ | Worst class share error ↓ | Tokens (input / output) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| as before · All rulings reused; an approved AI answer could outvote an engineer's correction | No AI model | 201 | 34/35 | 3.3 points | None (no AI call: replays stored results); run 5's own tokens are under section 53 |
| decisions only · Only the engineer's own decisions reused (29 lines); approved AI answers not | No AI model | 47 | 35/35 | 1.8 points | None (no AI call: replays stored results) |
| decisions first · All rulings reused, engineer decisions outrank approved AI answers (chosen) | No AI model | 201 | 35/35 | 1.8 points | None (no AI call: replays stored results) |

Decisions only would hand about 140 items per study back to the model (about 1.50 a study at run
5's prices). Decisions first keeps the 35/35 and the 201 served, with the blanket rows still in
place. Bryan chose it over decisions only.

**Change.** `CachedClassification.decided` (from the row's `result.method`), `ConventionIndex.match`
looks at decisions first at any tier, `promote_conventions` never replaces a decision with a model
answer, the provenance carries `origin`, and the rationale names the kind of row. Tests:
`tests/LEDGER.md`. The test runs' blanket rows are deleted from the dev database and the run 5
copy.

### 55.2 Built

`basis/report/vendors.py`: a profile per package, each a column mapping over the generic rows
(vendor headers in the vendor's order, its codes, its date format, its description limit), rendered

## 56. Per-user activity, the study library on the server, the audit completed, the firm's own history (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Can an engineer see what they did, can the library search, filter and sort on the server
instead of in the browser, does the audit list every engineer action, and is anything that happens to a
firm (an invitation, a role, a removal) recorded anywhere?

**What was built** (migration `0022`; docs/api/STUDY_LIBRARY.md, docs/api/TIMELINE_AND_AUDIT.md):

| Piece | Route | Design decision |
|---|---|---|
| Per-user activity | `GET /v1/me/activity` | The caller's own `study_events` rows across the studies of their firms, with the study's id and property name, newest first by `seq`. The cap is two things: 200 rows a page, and a 90-day window when `since` is absent; the response echoes the window it applied so a client pins it on the next page. `since` after `until` is an empty page, not an error. Served by a new `(actor_id, seq DESC)` index. |
| Library | `GET /v1/studies` | `q` (case-insensitive substring, LIKE wildcards literal), `status` (repeatable), `created_by`, `include_archived`, `sort` (`updated_desc` default, `created_desc`, `name_asc`), `total`. The keyset cursor encodes the sort it was issued under and the row's key, so a cursor replayed under another sort is 422 rather than a wrong page. The default order changed from newest to most recently updated, which is what the web app shows by default. `POST .../unarchive` (owner) restores the status the stage implies, `failed` while a failure is recorded. |
| Audit | `GET /v1/studies/{id}/audit` | Eight kinds added from the events the routes already write (intake and report answers set, upload confirmed, started, retry, cancel, archived, unarchived, signed). Paginated on `(at, seq, kind, entity_id)`: assembled from four tables, sorted, cut; `seq` keeps several events of one request in order. |
| Firm history | `GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/activity` (owner) | `org_events`, append-only like `study_events`, written by the repositories so the operator CLI and the API record alike and a refused request leaves nothing: `org.created`, `invitation.created/accepted/declined/revoked` (with why), `member.role_changed`, `member.removed` (with the invitations it revoked), `profile.set` (the fields changed, never the logo). |

**Not SQL, on purpose.** The audit page is cut in memory after a four-table assembly. One study's
engineer actions are bounded by what engineers did to it (tens to low hundreds), not by the pipeline's
output; a union of four row shapes would buy nothing at that size. `GET /v1/me/activity` and the firm
history are plain keyset queries.

**Verified.** 18 library tests (pages under each of the three sorts over colliding names and shuffled
update times have no gap or repeat and equal the one listing cut; a row inserted between pages is neither
skipped nor repeated; `%`, `_` and `\` in `q` are literal; archived hidden unless asked; unarchive restores
each of five statuses and records one event under three concurrent requests queued on the held row lock), 16 activity tests (own
events only, a left firm hidden, the 90-day default against events written 80 and 100 days ago, every
firm action through its real route with who did what, the CLI's rows as `system`, re-inviting after
expiry, `org_events` refusing UPDATE and DELETE, the last-owner refusal leaving no event), the audit's
eleven items in order with pages of four, migration `0022` up, constraints, down to the `0021` snapshot
and up again, `alembic check` clean, the OpenAPI document regenerated and the contract test (Schemathesis
over every operation, the three new ones included) green, every gate green.

**One guard moved under the lock (2026-11-01).** CI once recorded three `study.unarchived` events for
three concurrent unarchives (locally 2 of 20 rounds, with either rate-limit store). The route decided
"was archived" from the access dependency's read, taken before the repository's `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`;
three requests that all read `archived` before the first committed then serialized on the lock, the
second and third found the study restored, returned it unchanged, and still recorded an event because
their pre-lock read said it had been archived. The repository now reports whether it restored the study,
decided under the lock, and the route records exactly then. The test no longer relies on timing: it holds
the row locked while the three requests are sent, waits until all three are blocked on it
(`pg_stat_activity`), then releases; the old guard fails it every round, the new one passes it 20 of 20
with the in-memory and the Postgres limiter.

**And one the fuzz found after the merge with main.** `GET .../timeline?event_type=<NUL>` answered 500:
the timeline's filter was a plain `list[str]`, the NUL reached asyncpg, which refuses it. The activity
routes had the rule (non-empty, at most 100 characters, no NUL) from the start; it now lives in
`basis.api.routes.common.EventTypes` and the three routes share it (three new timeline cases, the
OpenAPI document regenerated).

**Not verified.** No live run through the stack: the routes are exercised against a real PostgreSQL in
the tests, not against the staging deployment; the web app is unchanged and still filters in the
browser (STUDY_LIBRARY.md section 5 maps each piece to the request). `localeCompare` and `lower()` may
order accented names differently. The audit's in-memory page is the right size for a study's engineer
actions; a study with thousands of corrections would want the union query.

## 57. Pre-launch security review of the backend: findings, fixes, what is verified (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Before an outside firm receives a link: can a caller reach anything without a token, see
or change another firm's data, exhaust the service, or read something the server should keep (a stack,
a path, a key)? Yardsticks: OWASP ASVS 5.0 (V4 access control, V8 data protection, V14.4 headers) and
the OWASP API Security Top 10 (API1 object-level authorization, API4 unrestricted resource consumption,
API8 misconfiguration). Each claim below names the test that proves it; what is not tested says so.

**Scope read.** `basis/auth/firebase.py`, `basis/api/{auth,users,app,ratelimit,errors,bodylimit,
middleware,idempotency,openapi,local_uploads}.py`, every module in `basis/api/routes/`, the request
schemas, `basis/config.py`, `basis/obs/logging.py`, the repositories' visibility methods, the
Dockerfile, `docker-compose*.yml`, `infra/staging/run.tf`, `.env.example`, `.gitleaksignore`,
`.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `tooling/check_no_client_data.py` and the CI workflow.

### 56.1 Findings

| # | Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | medium | Rate limits were counted per API process only. `basis/api/ratelimit.py` promised a Postgres-backed limiter ("S1-C") that did not exist anywhere in the tree; `create_app` always installed `InMemoryRateLimiter`. Cloud Run runs up to `api_max_instances` processes, so a caller's budget was the published limit times the instance count, and a scale-out under a flood raised the budget exactly when it mattered (API4). | **Fixed** (56.2) |
| 2 | low | No `Cache-Control` on `/v1` JSON responses and problems, and `X-Content-Type-Options` only on the four file routes. Every `/v1` answer is private to the token's bearer; RFC 9111 lets a private cache store a response to an `Authorization` request unless told otherwise (ASVS 8.3.1, 14.4.4). | **Fixed** (56.3) |
| 3 | low | `Content-Disposition` on `GET .../documents/{id}/pdf`: the report PDF's name is read from inside the uploaded UAD 3.6 ZIP, and the ASCII fallback kept a backslash or a control character and turned a quote into `'`; a CR or LF would have ended the header. A registered filename could never carry them (`FILENAME_PATTERN`); a ZIP entry can. No test covered a hostile name. | **Fixed** (56.4) |
| 4 | medium | `POST /v1/cost-indices` lets the owner of **any** firm append a value to the deployment-wide cost index store; the value then prices every firm's studies (the route's own description says so). With one firm this was a convenience; with a second firm it is one tenant changing another's pricing (API1/API5 by design). | **Deferred**: a product decision (operator-only through `OPS_OPERATOR_UIDS`, or a per-firm store); decide before the second firm is onboarded. |
| 5 | low | `check_revoked` is on in `prod` only (S1_SPEC 4): in `staging` a disabled or deleted Firebase user keeps access until the ID token expires (at most one hour). | Deferred: by specification, saves a Firebase read per request in staging. |
| 6 | low | `mask_reason` on a photo object whose SAM 3 box prompt failed carries the provider's URL path (query, hence the token, stripped) and up to 200 characters of the provider's error body, shown to the study's own engineers (`basis/api/routes/objects.py`, `tests/api/test_objects.py` asserts it). | Deferred: no secret in it, visible only inside the firm, useful to the engineer; change if a provider's error text ever carries account detail. |
| 7 | low | Unauthenticated requests are limited by `request.client.host`; on Cloud Run that is the front end, so every anonymous caller shares one address budget. Authenticated budgets are by verified uid and unaffected; the anonymous path answers 401 anyway. | Deferred: the fix is `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips` on uvicorn in the image, an infrastructure change outside this PR. |
| 8 | info | `/docs` and `/openapi.json` are public. The document holds no secret and the API is bearer-only. | Accepted (standard; `docs_url=None` in prod is a one-line change if wanted). |
| 9 | info | A user's `display_name` is taken from the token's `name` claim and stored unbounded; shown to the firm's other members. Bounded in practice by the header size uvicorn accepts (about 16 KiB), which was not tested. | Accepted; a frontend must escape it like any user text. |
| 10 | info | With Temporal not configured the workflow routes answer 503 `temporal-not-configured` before the study's access check runs (the same 503 for every id, so nothing is learned); with Temporal configured the check runs first. The isolation test therefore carries a fake workflow service. | Accepted. |

Nothing high. The two medium findings are the ones to act on before launch: 1 is fixed here, 4 is a
decision.

### 56.2 Fix 1: one budget per caller across every API process

`basis/api/ratelimit_pg.py`, `PostgresRateLimiter`: the same sliding-window log as the in-memory
limiter, kept in `rate_limit_hits` (migration `0023`, an `UNLOGGED` table: ephemeral state, no WAL per
request). Per hit, in one short transaction of its own: `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(key))`
serializes the key (so two concurrent requests cannot both read `limit - 1`), `now()` is the database
clock (instances agree), the key's expired rows are deleted, the rest counted; under the limit a row is
inserted, over it the answer carries `Retry-After` as the moment the oldest counted hit leaves the
window. A sweep every 60 s deletes idle keys' rows older than an hour. The alternatives considered:
GCRA or a token bucket in one row (O(1), but admits a full burst then a steady refill, which the
in-memory limiter's docstring rejects for being above the stated per-minute figure, and would have given
the two stores different semantics); a fixed-window counter (admits 2x at a boundary). The log keeps both
stores exact and identical, and at 240 reads per minute per user its cost is one row per request.

`RATE_LIMIT_STORE` (`basis/config.py`): `memory` or `postgres`; unset means `postgres` in `staging`
and `prod` and `memory` in `dev` and `test`; `memory` is **refused** in staging and prod
(`ConfigError`), and `postgres` without a database refuses to start (`create_app`). `install_database`
installs the limiter next to the Postgres idempotency store, so the lifespan-owned engine and the tests'
injected sessionmaker take the same path.

Degraded mode: when the database cannot be reached (connection refused, pool exhausted, connection
dropped) the limiter answers from a per-process `InMemoryRateLimiter` and logs one warning per minute
(`BASIS-API-044`, with `fallbacks`). Failing closed would turn a database outage into a refusal of every
request, including `GET /v1/ops/health`, which is built to answer while the database is down. A
`ProgrammingError` (the table missing because `0023` was not applied) is **not** caught: it surfaces as a
500 on the first request instead of silently falling back.

Proof: `tests/api/test_rate_limit.py` now runs all five route tests against both stores;
`tests/api/test_rate_limit_pg.py` (13 tests): two instances share one budget; 20 concurrent requests
against a budget of 5 admit exactly 5 (`asyncio.gather` across four limiter instances); a hit backdated
to 40 s ago gives `Retry-After` in (15, 20] and one past the window frees its slot and is deleted;
`Retry-After` is the oldest counted hit's expiry, not the whole window; the unreachable-database case
limits per process, counts `fallbacks` and warns once; the lifespan installs and shutdown removes it.
`tests/unit/config/test_rate_limit_store.py` (11 tests) covers the setting's defaults and refusals.
`tests/integration/db/test_migrations.py`: head `0023`, `alembic check` clean, `CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE`
in the offline SQL.

Not measured: the limiter's cost under load (one lock, one delete, one select and one insert per
`/v1` request). The load harness of section 31 can re-run against `RATE_LIMIT_STORE=postgres`.
Migration numbering: three sessions add migrations in parallel; it is `0023` here, after #110's `0022`.

### 56.3 Fix 2: response headers

`basis/api/headers.py`, `SecurityHeadersMiddleware`, between the request-id middleware and CORS so
error responses carry it too: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on every response; `Cache-Control:
no-store` on every `/v1` response that sets none itself (the file routes keep `private, max-age=3600`
and the preview `private, no-cache`); `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`
in `staging` and `prod` only. Proof: `tests/unit/api/test_security_headers.py` (13 tests: a body, a 401,
a 404, a 413, an opaque 500, a route's own policy kept, `/health` unmarked, HSTS by environment).

### 56.4 Fix 3: download filenames

`_content_disposition` in `basis/api/routes/documents.py`: the quoted fallback replaces every C0
control, DEL, `"` and `\` with `_` (non-ASCII stays `?`), an empty name becomes `file`, and the ZIP
entry's name is split on both separators. `filename*` already percent-encoded everything outside the
unreserved set, so the original name survives there. Proof: `tests/unit/api/test_content_disposition.py`
(8 cases including `x\r\nX-Injected: 1.pdf`, a backslash, a lone quote, NUL and DEL); the two existing
header tests in `test_document_content.py` are unchanged.

### 56.5 Verified safe, with the test that proves it

| Area | What holds | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Token checks | The Firebase Admin SDK checks the RS256 signature against Google's certificates, `aud` and `iss` against the project id, `exp`/`iat`/`auth_time`; expired, revoked, disabled, deleted, invalid and no-subject tokens each map to a distinct 401 detail that never includes the SDK's message; certificate fetch failure is 503, not 401 | `tests/unit/auth/test_firebase_verifier.py` (the real SDK against bad, expired and emulator tokens; audience checked even with the emulator) |
| Emulator guard | `FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST` with `BASIS_ENV` staging or prod is a `ConfigError` at `create_app`; a blank variable is "not set" | `test_emulator_refused_in_deployed_envs`, `test_app_refuses_to_start_with_emulator_in_deployed_envs` |
| No route without a token | All 55 documented operations other than `GET /health` and `GET /` answer 401 (`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`) to no token and to a rejected token, with `{}` as the body so a 422 cannot mask a missing check, and create no user | `tests/api/test_auth.py::test_every_documented_operation_needs_a_token` (new) |
| Header parsing | Missing, non-Bearer, empty, two-token and case-variant headers; verification once per request, in a worker thread | `tests/api/test_auth_dependency.py` |
| Verified email for invitations | Accepting or declining with an unverified email is 403 `email-unverified`; another email is 404; `GET /v1/me` lists pending invitations only for a verified email | `tests/api/test_firms.py` |
| Tenant isolation | Every one of the 47 operations whose path names a study, a firm or an invitation answers 404 to a member of another firm, byte-identical (minus `request_id`, `instance`) to the 404 for an id that does not exist; a member's own study or firm in the path does not reach another firm's document, photo, object, member or invitation; a filter by another study's asset returns nothing | `tests/api/test_tenancy.py` (new; `BODIES` must list every scoped operation, so a new scoped route fails until listed) |
