## 58. Leaving a study and coming back: gate drafts on the server, resumable uploads, restarting a cancelled study (2026-11-01)

**Question.** An engineer who leaves a study at any stage must be able to come back and continue
with nothing lost. What is lost today, and what does the backend need so that nothing is?

**What was lost, verified in the frontend.** `web/live/live-review.js:24` keeps the corrections
an engineer adds at a gate in `L.corrections` (a `Map` per stage) until `POST .../decisions`
sends them; `live-app.js:105,149,215` keeps the upload run in `L.upload`. Both are tab memory:
a reload, a closed tab or a switch of study drops them. After a reload a draft study showed
"Ready to start" with no way to add its files, and the upload screen always created a new
study. A third gap was in the backend itself: `POST .../cancel` ends the execution and nothing
can start the study again (`start` answers 409 `workflow-closed` for ever, because the one
workflow id per study is reused with `REJECT_DUPLICATE`), so a cancelled study could only be
archived and re-created by hand.

**Built** (docs/api/GATE_DRAFTS_AND_RESUME.md; PR this section ships in):

1. *Gate drafts.* `GET`/`PUT`/`DELETE /v1/studies/{id}/drafts/{stage}` (engineer): one
   document per study, stage and user (`review_drafts`, migration 0024) with the pending
   `comment` and `corrections`, the `revision` they name rows of, and a `version` that is its
   `ETag`/`If-Match` exactly as the intake's. The `PUT` runs the decision route's own checks
   (type for the stage, target in the revision, values, reasons, removals, added fields), so a
   draft that would be refused at submit time is refused at save time with the same `errors`.
   A draft whose revision the study has left, or whose stage was decided at that revision, is
   returned with `stale: true` and the reason, never as current. The decision deletes the
   submitting engineer's draft in its own transaction (`review.decided` records
   `draft_discarded`). Two engineers draft apart; `GET` lists whose other drafts exist (who,
   since when, how many), not their content.
2. *Resumable uploads.* The registration already survived a reload (`GET /v1/studies/{id}`
   lists the document with `uploaded_at: null` and its sha256); what was missing was the signed
   URL, which only the first response carried and which expires in 15 minutes. `POST
   .../documents/{id}/upload-url` re-issues it for an unconfirmed document (409
   `upload-complete` for a confirmed one, whose bytes are immutable). A repeated `POST
   .../documents` for the same bytes stays the 409 `duplicate-document` that names the
   document: the route is not idempotent on sha256 in the replay sense, and it need not be,
   since the client matches a re-selected file to its registration by sha256 from the study's
   document list. The resume sequence is written out for the frontend.
3. *Cancelled studies.* `POST /v1/studies/{id}/restart` (owner): the execution is described
   first (RUNNING is 409 `workflow-running`, COMPLETED 409 `study-completed`; cancelled,
   terminated, timed out, failed before v0.9, or gone after retention proceed); one transaction
   resets the row to `extracting` on revision + 1 with the failure cleared (`stage.entered`,
   `study.restarted`); then a new execution starts under the same `study-{id}` with
   `ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY`, so `studies.workflow_id`, the relay's routing, `cancel` and
   `retry` keep working. The new revision keeps the cancelled run's rows as history and makes
   every draft for them stale. Two restarts racing, or a 503 after the reset: the row lock
   serializes the resets and the second reuses the first's (it finds the `study.restarted`
   event with no `run.started` after it), one start wins, the other is 409 `workflow-running`,
   and the row is at the revision the running execution was given.

**Why no `draft.saved` / `draft.discarded` timeline events.** The timeline is the record of
what happened to the study and the audit trail of the engineer input that changed it. A draft
changes nothing about the study; its corrections enter the trail as `correction.recorded` when
the decision is submitted; it is saved on every edit (an append-only row per autosave would
bury the trail and keep every half-typed value for ever) and deleted when submitted or
discarded. `review.decided` carries `draft_discarded`; who is drafting since when is on the row.

**Verified** (every gate green on the branch; `tests/LEDGER.md`): 20 draft tests (+ 6
malformed-body cases) including three concurrent first saves and three concurrent saves with
one tag each ending with exactly one 200; 6 resume tests including the documented sequence end
to end against the local storage; 7 restart tests on the fake Temporal including the 503 and
the concurrent double restart; 3 service tests on the id policies; migration 0024 from an
empty database (the stage check compares the label as text, because `components_review` is a
new enum value in the same transaction and PostgreSQL refuses an unsafe use of it) and back.
The OpenAPI document carries the five operations and the Schemathesis contract test runs them
(the draft `PUT` gets the intake's carve-out: `If-Match` dropped, since a generated tag is
rightly 412).

**Not verified.** The restart against a real Temporal server and worker (the fake answers the
id policies as the real one does; the service unit test pins the policies sent). What the new
execution does with a study whose revision 1 rows exist (ingest's "already published" branch
and the per-revision unique keys say it writes revision 2 apart, as a rejection does) has not
been run live. The frontend changes (reading the draft on open, autosaving on edit, the
"continue this study" upload screen) are Bryan's.

**Open.** Whether a pending registration should be removable (not provided: a pending row
costs nothing and keeps the duplicate check honest); whether `others` should carry the drafts'
content for a reviewer role (not now: a colleague's half-finished work is theirs to send).

## 59. Firm onboarding from the API: invitation emails, self-service firms, names on studies (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Can an engineering firm get onto Basis from a link, with no operator at a terminal:
create its firm, invite its people, and have them told? Before this, a firm existed only through
`python -m basis.admin`, and an invitation was silent (`delivery: not_sent`).

**The standard, and what was taken from it.**
- Transactional email frameworks separate the message from the transport: Django renders an
  `EmailMessage` and hands it to the backend `EMAIL_BACKEND` names (`console` logs, `locmem` keeps
  it in memory, `smtp` sends); Rails' `ActionMailer` does the same with `delivery_method`. Basis
  now has `basis.email`: `EmailMessage` in, `EmailSender.send` out, chosen by `EMAIL_PROVIDER`
  (`log`, the default; `smtp` through the standard library; an HTTP provider is the documented
  slot).
- Providers that offer idempotent sends key them per intended send (Resend's `Idempotency-Key`,
  kept 24 hours; a key shared across recipients sends once to the first). Basis keys each
  invitation row (`invitation-{id}`); SMTP gets it as the `Message-ID`.
- The transactional outbox the relay already runs (claims with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, retries
  `min(2**attempts, 300)` s, dead after 50) is reused as the queue: the invitation is a
  `notification` of type `invitation`, enqueued in the transaction that inserts the invitation.

**Design.** `docs/api/FIRMS.md`. In short: `POST /v1/orgs` (verified email; the creator is the
owner; several firms per user allowed; names not unique), `PATCH /v1/orgs/{id}` (owner renames),
the invitation email through the outbox with its outcome on the invitation (`emailed_at`,
`email_error`; `delivery` derived: `queued`, `sent`, `failed`, `not_sent`), `created_by_name` and
`created_by_email` on studies, `signed_by_name` and `signed_by_email` on signatures; `org.created` and
`org.renamed` on the firm's history (section 56). Migration 0025
adds three nullable columns to `invitations`. Study visibility within a firm is unchanged and the
reasons are written down (FIRMS.md 7).

**Measured.**

| | |
|---|---|
| unit tests added | 48 (`tests/unit/email` 21, `tests/unit/config/test_email_settings.py` 20, relay 7) |
| integration tests added | 10 (`tests/integration/relay/test_invitation_emails.py`) |
| API tests added | 17 in `test_firms.py`; shape assertions widened in `test_studies.py`, `test_report_signing.py`, `test_health.py`, the CLI and migration tests |
| same transaction | a rolled-back create leaves neither row; a refused create (409) enqueues nothing |
| once per invitation | a second poll and a duplicate outbox row for an emailed invitation send nothing; `emailed_at` is written once |
| retries | a failing sender: outbox `attempts` 1, `email_error` set, `delivery: failed`; the next success clears it; three failures at `max_attempts=3` dead-letter; a 5xx recipient is dead at once |
| not sent when moot | an invitation revoked before the relay ran: the row is delivered unsent, both rows say why |
| SMTP | one session against a local server: From, To, Subject, deterministic `Message-ID`, `Auto-Submitted`; 550 final, 450 retried, refused connection retried |
| contract | `POST /v1/orgs` and `PATCH /v1/orgs/{org_id}` in `docs/api/openapi.json`; Schemathesis ran both with no carve-out |

**Decisions worth defending.**
- *Why the relay sends and the API only enqueues.* The API's transaction must not wait on a mail
  server, and a send that happened for an invitation that then rolled back cannot be unsent. The
  outbox gives exactly the ordering we need: commit first, send after, retry on failure.
- *Why `delivery: sent` with the log provider.* The sender accepted the message; what the sender
  does is the deployment's choice and is visible in `GET /v1/ops/health`'s relay row and the relay
  log. Reporting `not_sent` would make a firm's owner chase an email that was never meant to go.
- *Why no `visibility` column yet.* A stored field nothing enforces misleads the client; the rule is
  a product decision for the firms being pitched (FIRMS.md 7). `created_by_name` lets the app offer
  the "My studies" filter client-side meanwhile.
- *Why SMTP and not a provider SDK.* Every provider offers an SMTP relay; the standard library
  needs no account, no dependency and no key in the repository. The HTTP slot is documented for
  when bounce webhooks are wanted.

**Not verified here.**
- No email was sent to a real mailbox: no provider is configured in any environment
  (`EMAIL_PROVIDER=log` everywhere). The SMTP sender was exercised against a local server written in
  the test, not against a provider's relay with TLS and authentication.
- The frontend still says "No email is sent" and has no create-a-firm screen; `web/README.md`
  "Gaps" lists what the app does not show yet.
- The migration was written as 0024 on 0021 and renumbered 0025 on 0024 once user activity (0022),
  rate-limit hits (0023) and review drafts (0024) merged into this branch.

## 60. Backups, a retention rule, and alerts before firms use Basis (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Before a firm uploads client files: can a lost database or a deleted file be
recovered, can the firm bound how long its files stay, and does someone hear when a worker
dies or a study fails?

**Standard first.** Cloud SQL: daily automated backups plus point-in-time recovery from
write-ahead logs (Enterprise edition keeps 1 to 7 days; PITR always restores into a new
instance with `gcloud sql instances clone --point-in-time`; a backup restore overwrites its
target). GCS: object versioning with lifecycle rules on noncurrent versions, and soft delete
(7 days by default) under it; a deleted version is restored by copying `object#generation`
back. Cloud Monitoring: an uptime check with the policy the console generates for it
(`check_passed`, `ALIGN_NEXT_OLDER` over 20 min, `REDUCE_COUNT_FALSE`, more than one failed
probe); a ratio condition for 5xx; `condition_matched_log` for a log-based alert with a
notification rate limit; `cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up` for the database. Email:
render and transport split (Django's `EmailBackend`, Rails' delivery methods), one
idempotency key per intended send. Retention: a per-tenant rule applied by a job that keeps
the records of what it deleted (the pattern of every records-retention policy: the deletion
log outlives the deleted thing).

**What is plan-only (nothing applied; staging stays parked).** `infra/staging/sql.tf`: PITR on
with 7 days of logs, 30 backups kept (`retention_unit = COUNT`), both deletion guards already
on. `storage.tf`: versioning on the uploads bucket, noncurrent versions deleted after 30 days
and capped at 10 per object, soft delete stated at 7 days, the staging-only 90-day rule kept
on live objects. `alerts.tf`: an email notification channel from a variable, an uptime check on
`/health` with its policy, API 5xx ratio above 5 % for 5 min (inactive without traffic), worker
pool instance count below 1 for 5 min (or absent), Cloud SQL `database/up` below 1, and a
log-based policy on `BASIS-WF-` codes except WF-010/011 (one notification per 5 min); all
created only with `-var alerts_enabled=true`, because a parked staging fails every one.
`RUNBOOK.md`: the restore commands (PITR clone, backup restore, noncurrent and soft-deleted
object restore), the purge job and its documented-not-enabled schedule, and the alert table.

Verified: `terraform fmt -check` and `terraform validate` (hashicorp/google 8.7.0); a read-only
`terraform plan -lock=false` against the real parked state: **0 to add, 3 to change, 0 to
destroy**: the Cloud SQL instance (`point_in_time_recovery_enabled false -> true`,
`retained_backups 7 -> 30`; `transaction_log_retention_days` already 7), the uploads bucket
(versioning, the two noncurrent rules, `with_state = LIVE` on the 90-day rule), and one
pre-existing drift unrelated to this change (`desired_status = TERMINATED` on the Temporal VM,
STAGING.md 5.5). The alert resources do not appear because `alerts_enabled` defaults to
false. The metric types and resource types were read from the project's metric descriptors:
`run.googleapis.com/container/instance_count` applies to `cloud_run_worker_pool` (label
`state`), `request_count` carries `response_code_class`, `cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/up`
is a GAUGE INT64. Not verified: no apply, no restore drill, no alert fired, and whether Cloud
SQL accepts the PITR change while the instance is stopped (the runbook says what to do if it
refuses).

**Retention (backend, tested).** `orgs.retention_days` (null keeps everything), set by an owner
with `PUT /v1/orgs/{org_id}/retention`, read by members. `python -m basis.retention purge
[--dry-run]` selects completed or archived studies of firms with a rule whose row last changed
more than the rule ago, lists the study's prefix in storage (`Storage.list`, new on the
protocol), deletes every object except `exports/` (export JSON, assets CSV, calls transcript,
report PDF and schedule, signed report), keeps every database row, sets `studies.purged_at`
and appends `study.purged` with the counts; objects first, mark and event after, so a crash
leaves work for the next run and never an unrecorded deletion. Migration
`0026_retention_alerts` (revises `0025_invitation_email`). docs/api/RETENTION_AND_ALERTS.md.

**Alerts (backend, tested).** `record_failure` enqueues one `alert` notification per failure in
the transaction that writes `stage.failed`, keyed by the activity's key; the relay checks
`service_heartbeats` every 60 s and enqueues one per service per stale period (newest
heartbeat older than 300 s; keyed by that heartbeat, `never` for a service with no row). An
`alerts` table with a unique key makes the second raise of the same occurrence a no-op. The
relay renders the alert (`basis.notify.render`) and hands it to the `EmailSender`
of section 59 (`basis.email`: `EMAIL_PROVIDER` log or SMTP, shared with the invitation
emails) addressed to `ALERT_EMAIL_TO`, with the key as the idempotency key; unset,
the alert goes to the log at WARNING. Transient sender errors retry with the relay's backoff,
a refused recipient dead-letters.

**Tests** (all on PostgreSQL where they touch the database): the selection, the dry run, the
exact set deleted and kept, the no-op second run, an object already gone, a storage failure,
the CLI's output and exit status; a failed study enqueues exactly one alert and a retried
activity none more; one alert per service per stale period, one per service, `never`, the
newest instance counting; the relay sends once and a redelivery reuses the key; the route's
access rules and validation. Unit: the listing, the rendering, the sender boundary, the
relay's outcomes. Gates green: ruff, format, mypy, the catalogue and OpenAPI checks, the rule
fingerprints, pytest (unit and integration), the client-data guard.

**Open.** The SMTP transport and `EMAIL_PROVIDER`/`EMAIL_FROM` come with the firm-admin branch;
until it lands alerts are logged. A recovery notice ("worker back") is not sent. Firm owners
are not emailed about their own failed studies (operator only). Scheduling the purge is a
documented gcloud step, not Terraform, by decision (staging parked, no firm has a rule yet).

## 61. Reopening a completed study, the revision history, restoring a revision (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Once a study is `completed` nothing could take it back to a gate. Bryan wants a
Google-Docs-like history: reopen a completed study at a chosen step (the later steps recompute,
with a warning), see every version with who, when and what changed, and restore an older
version as a new one. The design is docs/api/REVISIONS.md; this section records what was
decided, what was measured and what is not verified.

### 59.1 The standard

Versioned document systems append, they never undo: Git's `revert` is a new commit, a Wikipedia
undo is a new revision, Google Docs' and Notion's "restore this version" make the chosen
version current and keep the later ones in the history. Temporal cannot continue a closed
execution (no signal or update reaches it), and among its id-reuse policies only
`ALLOW_DUPLICATE` admits a new execution under an id whose last one completed
(`ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY`, which `restart` uses, refuses it); a running execution is the
conflict policy's business. So reopen and restore each add a revision and start a new execution
under the study's one workflow id.

### 59.2 Decisions a reviewer may ask about

* **What a reopen keeps** is exactly what the chosen gate shows (REVISIONS.md section 2):
  through the rooms review the extraction, rooms, assignments, per-photo components and
  objects; the components review adds the reconciled inventories; the assets review adds the
  assets with takeoffs, costs and citations. Everything after the gate recomputes. The room
  inventories are left out below the components review because they are the room step's
  output, rebuilt from the grouping the engineer approves (what a rooms rejection does); the
  assets are copied, not recomputed, at the assets review because the gate must show what was
  approved (recomputing could reprice with a newer index and spend on the classifier).
* **A new execution, not a continued one**, with the gate and the copied revision in the
  input (`StudyWorkflowInput.resume`). The lifecycle was split into gate segments
  (`_appraisal_gate`, `_rooms_gates`, `_components_review_gate`, `_assets_gate_and_export`)
  with the command order unchanged: the five recorded histories replay, so no patch marker.
  The copy is the workflow's first activity (`carry_revision`, one transaction, idempotent,
  heartbeating), not the API's transaction, for the same reason `apply_corrections` is one.
* **Concurrency.** The route describes the execution before writing (running: 409), moves the
  row under its lock, and starts with conflict `FAIL`: Temporal admits one of two concurrent
  starts. A reset whose start did not happen (503, or in flight in the other request) is
  reused by a repeat of the same request, found from the timeline (the last resume event at
  the current revision with no `run.started` after it) exactly as `restart` does.
* **The history and the diff read what exists** (`study_events`, `reviews`, `corrections`,
  `report_signatures`, the rows' `carried_from`): no new table, no migration. The diff pairs
  rows by their **lineage root** rather than by "the ancestor at revision a": for successive
  revisions the two are the same; after a restore (whose rows descend from the restored
  revision and skip the ones between) only the root pairs a row with its counterpart, so the
  diff 3 → 4 of a revision 4 restored from 1 shows revision 3's changes undone. The first
  version used the ancestor and the lifecycle round trip caught it.
* **Restore opens at the last gate the revision reached** (its `stage.entered` rows; its rows
  when it predates the timeline), copies through that gate, and refuses the current revision
  (`revision-current`) and one that never reached a gate (`revision-not-restorable`). A reopen
  and a restore both need a `completed` study: a study at a gate is changed by rejecting there.
* **Not carried, on purpose:** nothing is re-analyzed, re-localized or re-voted by the copy;
  a photo the engineer wants re-analyzed is flagged at the components review as always.
* Codes `BASIS-STUDY-030..034`; `workflow-running` is now shared with the restart's refusal
  (each raise passes its code; the restart's is the generic). No migration (#114's `0024` is
  the latest; the brief's `0027` is not needed).

### 59.3 Verified

| What | Where | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Reopen at each of the four gates on the Temporal test server: the second execution's activity sequence, the gate open on revision 2 with the copy (assets only at the assets review), completion at revision 2 with its own export, revision 1's export bytes, signature and rows untouched, two runs under one id, the timeline events | `tests/lifecycle/test_reopen.py` (4 cases) | pass |
| Restore round trip: 1 → reopen (2) → rename rejection (3) → restore 1 (4): revision 4 has revision 1's rooms, diff 1 → 4 empty, diff 3 → 4 the rename undone, the history's four origins, three distinct exports | same (1) | pass |
| Two starts at once over the completed execution: Temporal admits exactly one | same (1) | pass |
| The recorded histories still replay after the lifecycle refactor | `tests/lifecycle/test_versioning.py` | pass |
| `carry_revision` per gate on rows the real activities wrote (inventories, assets, localizations, objects), idempotent, revision 1 untouched | `tests/unit/activities/test_carry_revision.py` (4) | pass |
| Every refusal, the dry run, the concurrent and racing reopens, the reused reset, restore, the history (with and without a timeline), the diff with its pagination and reverse | `tests/api/test_revisions.py` (27) | pass |
| Tenancy walk and route inventory with the four routes; the OpenAPI contract fuzz | `test_tenancy.py`, `test_health.py`, `test_openapi_contract.py` | pass |

Two defects the tests found before the PR: the activity copied the localized objects twice
(`_carry_rooms` already carries them; the lifecycle run hit `pk_photo_localizations`), and the
resumed workflow pre-set its stage to the gate, so the status query said `awaiting` before the
gate's transition had run (a client polling for it would have seen the gate before the row was
open); the initial stage is `uploading` as for every execution.

### 59.4 Not verified

A reopen through a deployed API and worker (the API tests use the fake Temporal, the lifecycle
tests bypass the API; the two halves are the same code as `restart`'s, whose live path is also
unverified). The room step on a reopened study with `ROOM_RECONCILE` on (the suite pins it
off, so the inventories' rebuild after a rooms-review reopen is exercised only by
`test_carry_revision.py`'s "left behind" case, not by a live room call). The frontend (the
warning from `dry_run`, the history view, the diff view) is Bryan's.

**Open.** Extraction fields in the diff (the audit and `provenance` cover them); a reopen of a
study whose execution predates the components gate runs the current flow and the API keeps its
manual edits at the gate the new execution has (documented, not tested); whether a restore
should be allowed while the study waits at a gate (it would have to cancel the execution).

## 62. Races and edge cases before firms use it: two people on one study, nothing changes a final study silently (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Bryan's two conditions before an engineering firm works in Basis: two people acting
on the same study at once must never corrupt it, and nothing may change a study that is already
final without saying so. A read-only audit of main `f7d2c50` found the API's happy paths and error
codes covered and six races tested (two decisions on one gate, two intake writes, double unarchive,
owners demoting each other, cancel mid-step, stale-revision decisions). This section takes the paths
that audit left untested, writes one deterministic test per path, fixes what the tests expose, and
says for each whether the code was **verified safe** or **fixed**.

**Method.** Every race is made real, never left to timing. Two patterns: `dbtest_support.race`
(S1_SPEC 7: each contender in its own transaction, released together by a barrier, the winner holding
its transaction open so the loser really waits), and the new `dbtest_support.queued_behind_a_lock`,
which generalizes the double-unarchive test of section 56: the test holds the contested row's lock (or
a table lock), starts each request only once the previous one is seen waiting on it in
`pg_stat_activity`, then releases. Every request has then read what it reads before the lock while
the row was still in its initial state, and PostgreSQL grants the lock to its waiters in queue order,
so the test chooses who wins. A request that never waits on the lock fails the test, which is itself
the finding (the code under test does not take the lock). Each test was run against a deliberately
broken version before it was kept; the break is named in each row. The Temporal cases run on the
time-skipping test server with the real activities (`tests/lifecycle`), the archive rule with the
real API over that server's client.

### 62.1 Findings

| # | Path | Verdict | What holds, and the test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Two `POST .../report/sign` at once | **verified safe** | `sign_report` takes the study's row lock before any check; the second re-reads under it, finds the signature and is 409 `BASIS-REPORT-009` before it renders or stores: one row, one signed PDF, one event. Broken (no `FOR UPDATE` in `lock_study`): both render and store, the second insert is a 500 on the unique key and leaves an orphan PDF. `test_report_signing.py::test_two_signings_at_once_record_one_signature_and_one_pdf` |
| 2 | Two `POST .../documents` with one sha256 | **verified safe** | Nothing is locked before the insert; released together from a table lock, the unique key `(study_id, sha256)` arbitrates: one 201, the other waits on the key, fails inside its savepoint and is 409 `duplicate-document` naming the winner; one row; only the winner got an upload URL. Which one wins is the index's choice, so the test is order-free. Broken (the unique constraint dropped in the test database): both 201, two rows. `test_uploads.py::test_two_registrations_of_one_sha256_at_once_create_one_document` |
| 3 | Two `promote_conventions` of one firm on one key | **verified safe** | `put` and `confirm` lock the row (`FOR UPDATE`) before reading `approvals`; two activity bodies for two studies released by a barrier both answer `confirmed` and the row goes 1 -> 3 with the seeding study kept and one event per study (approvals 2 and 3); at the repository, `put`+`put`, `put`+`confirm`, `confirm`+`confirm` go 3, 5, 7. Learned from the broken versions: without the lock in `put`, two `put`s still end right, because the `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` makes PostgreSQL's unique check wait on the in-flight transaction holding the row, so the second read sees the first's commit; but a `put` racing a `confirm` reads before the `confirm` locks and the row ends at 4 instead of 5 (the repository test fails on it). The promote test, two `put`s, was proved against a `put` with neither the lock nor the insert on the existing-row path (a read-then-write): both read 1, both write 2. `node/test_promote_race.py`, `integration/db/test_classification_cache.py::test_two_approvals_of_one_convention_at_once_both_count` |
| 4 | Two `PUT /orgs/{id}/profile` and two `PUT .../report-answers` with one `If-Match` | **verified safe** | The precondition is checked under the firm's (the study's) row lock against the version read there: 200 (version 2) and 412 with `ETag "2"` (`BASIS-REPORT-011`, `-012`); the loser's document is not written; the answers' timeline shows versions 1 and 2 only. Broken (the precondition checked against the route's unlocked read): both 200, version 3. `test_report_signing.py::test_two_profile_writes_with_one_etag_at_once_write_one`, `::test_two_answers_writes_with_one_etag_at_once_write_one` |
| 5 | Archive while the workflow runs or waits at a gate | **fixed** (62.2) | `DELETE /v1/studies/{id}` archived a running study: its next transition then failed the execution (every transition refuses an archived study), and one at a gate waited for a decision the API refuses. Now 409 `workflow-running` (`BASIS-STUDY-035`) while Temporal says `RUNNING`; cancel first. On the real workflow: refused in progress and at the gate, 200 once the cancel closed the execution, recorded once; a decision after the archive is 409 from the API and refused by the closed execution; unarchived, the study reads `waiting_review` with a `CANCELED` execution and `restart` is the path. `lifecycle/test_archive_rule.py`, `test_workflow_routes.py::test_archive_is_refused_while_the_execution_runs`, `::test_archive_of_a_started_study_needs_temporal` |
| 6 | `POST .../retry` pressed twice on the real workflow | **verified safe** | With the clearing `record_failure` held open by the test (so the window between the first retry and the stage's restart is real), two more retries answer `already_requested: true` and start nothing: one `:retry1` extraction, two calls in all, the study completes; a retry after the restart is `InvalidRetry`. Broken (the ack's `already_requested` always false): the second reads false. `lifecycle/test_stage_retry.py::test_a_second_retry_before_the_stage_restarts_is_already_requested` |
| 7 | An execution ending `failed` through `_record_end("failed")` | **fixed** (62.3) | The run was recorded `failed` while the study row stayed `processing` at its stage with no reason: a client polling the study saw it in progress forever. Now the workflow records the failure on the study first. `lifecycle/test_failed_end.py` |
| 8 | Intake, report answers and firm profile after the study started or the report was signed | **fixed** (62.4) | `PUT .../intake` refused only archived studies: the price, the dates and the land method could change during the run, after completion and after signing, with nothing marking the result, the export or the signed report stale. Now 409 `intake-locked` (`BASIS-STUDY-036`) from the start on. The answers and the profile stay writable after signing (the profile serves every study); the signed PDF never changes (verified: the bytes are identical after both writes), and `report/state` now says which inputs changed since the signature. `test_studies.py::test_the_intake_is_locked_once_the_study_has_started`, `test_report_signing.py::test_inputs_written_after_signing_are_reported_not_rendered`, `::test_an_answers_write_queued_before_the_signing_makes_it_412` |

Broken (no `expected_workflow_id`): the archive lands. `test_workflow_routes.py::test_a_start_and_an_archive_at_once_leave_the_study_running` |

| 9c | Two `DELETE` (archive) at once, or a repeat | **fixed** (62.2) | The route recorded `study.archived` on every request, including on a study already archived: the mirror of the unarchive defect of section 56. Broken (the event recorded unconditionally): two events. `test_study_library.py::test_concurrent_archives_record_one_event` |
| 9d | Two `POST .../documents/{id}/complete` at once | **fixed** (62.2) | Both confirmations verify the object (it is immutable) and both reached the compare-and-set; the one that lost it still recorded `document.uploaded`, so one upload had two events. Now `confirm_upload` says which call set `uploaded_at` and only that one records. Broken (recorded unconditionally): two events. `test_uploads.py::test_two_confirmations_of_one_upload_at_once_record_one_event` |
| 9e | An answers write queued before a signing | **verified safe** | The signing renders under the lock from the new answers, the reviewed preview is no longer the report: 412 `BASIS-REPORT-010` with the current tag, nothing signed, the answer kept. `test_report_signing.py::test_an_answers_write_queued_before_the_signing_makes_it_412` |

### 62.2 The archive rule

Decided from `docs/api/WORKFLOW.md` and the repositories: `StudyRepository.transition`,
`WorkflowStateRepository.converge` and `mark_failed` all refuse an archived study, and `unarchive`
restores the status the stage implies. So an archive must happen only when nothing runs for the
study, or the execution dies at its next step (or waits forever at a gate) and an unarchive brings
back a study whose execution is gone. The two candidate rules were to cancel on the owner's behalf or
to refuse. Refusing was chosen: a cancel is an explicit, recorded act (`study.cancel_requested` with
its reason) and `POST .../restart` (PR #114) is built on an execution the owner closed knowingly; a
soft delete that silently cancels would hide that choice.

`DELETE /v1/studies/{id}` (`basis/api/routes/studies.py`): one short transaction for the access
check, then, when the study has a `workflow_id` and is not archived already, `describe` on the
workflow service with no transaction open (as the workflow routes do); `RUNNING` is 409
`workflow-running` `BASIS-STUDY-035`, an execution Temporal no longer knows is over, Temporal not
configured or unreachable is 503 (a draft asks nothing and archives). Then a second transaction:
`StudyRepository.archive(study_id, expected_workflow_id=<what the route read>)` takes the row lock,
returns `Archived(study, archived)` (`archived=False` on a repeat, which records nothing) and raises
`StaleStateError` when the `workflow_id` changed since the read (a start landed in between), which the
route answers with the same 409. `docs/api/STUDY_LIBRARY.md` section 4 has the rule and its edges.

`DocumentRepository.confirm_upload` is the same shape for uploads (`Confirmed(document,
confirmed)`); `mark_uploaded` keeps its signature for the callers that do not care.

### 62.3 An execution that ends failed

Patch `failed-end-records-failure-v1` in `StudyWorkflow.run`: when the lifecycle task raises
something no stage held (the photo listing failing permanently, a transition the API outran, an
unexpected exception), `_record_failed` sets the status query's `failed_stage`, `failure` and
`failure_code` and runs `record_failure` for the study's stage and revision (the reason and code from
`_failure`, the same mapping the holds use; for a non-activity exception `BASIS-WF-...` unexpected
with the exception's text), then `_record_end("failed")` as before. A failure to record it is logged,
never raised: the end is still recorded. The test fails `list_photos` with a non-retryable
`SimulatedFailure`: the execution closes `FAILED`, the row is `failed` at `extracting` with
`failure_reason` `list_photos: SimulatedFailure: ... [BASIS-WF-...]` and the matching
`failure_code`, the closed execution's status query says the same, `TemporalWorkflowService.retry` is
`WorkflowNotRunningError` (the route's 409 `workflow-closed`), the run is `failed`, the last three
activities are `list_photos`, `record_failure`, `record_run_end`, the timeline has `stage.failed`
(`marked` true) then `run.ended`, and the history replays. Without the patch the row stays
`processing` with no reason (the test fails on the status). The recorded histories of
`tests/lifecycle/histories` replay unchanged (none ends failed). `docs/api/WORKFLOW.md` has the
client's view: retry is refused, restart runs the study again.

### 62.4 Inputs that feed a final output

**Research.** Systems that version inputs feeding a committed output do not edit the input in place:
accounting packages close a period and require an explicit reopen to change anything dated inside it
(QuickBooks' closing date, SAP's posting periods); e-signature services keep a signed envelope's
documents immutable and send a corrected document as a new envelope; a tagged release is never
rewritten, a new one is cut. The common shape: the output's inputs are frozen at the point the
output is derived, the output records what it was derived from, and a change is a new version with
its own derivation.

**The intake.** `POST .../start` is already the point where the engineer commits the inputs (it
refuses an incomplete intake, section 37). From then on the intake is read by the run and priced into
every output: cost year, location factor and property class into each cost row's trail, the basis into
the result, `summary.basis` of the export, the report, and once signed a PDF that cannot change. The
pricing records the intake version it used, so a stale pricing could be detected, but a signed report
could not. Rule: `StudyRepository.write_intake` raises `IntakeLockedError` when the study is not
`uploading`; the route answers 409 `intake-locked` `BASIS-STUDY-036` with the reopen as the path
(`docs/api/STUDY_RESULT.md`, "Locked once the study starts"). The lock is decided under the study's
row lock, so it holds against a concurrent start (9b). The reopen that landed meanwhile
(`POST .../reopen`, section 61) takes a completed study back to a gate on its last revision's rows and
keeps the intake, and `restart` reruns a cancelled study on the intake as it is: neither takes a new
intake, so today a started study's intake does not change at all. That is the safe side of the rule;
the reopen that accepts new inputs is the open item (docs/api/STUDY_RESULT.md, "Open"). The web client's intake form was
not changed here; after the start it will receive this 409 (noted for `web/`).

**The answers and the firm profile after signing.** They stay writable (the profile is firm-wide;
the answers may be corrected for the next revision) and the signed PDF is stored, so they cannot
change it; what was missing was the state saying so. Migration `0027_signature_input_versions` adds
`firm_profile_version` and `report_answers_version` to `report_signatures` (nullable: a signature
recorded before them); `sign_report` records the versions it rendered with, under the same lock as the
render, and puts them in the `report.signed` event's detail; `GET .../report/state` answers
`changed_since_signing` (`[]`, `["study"]`, `["firm"]`, both; `null` while unsigned or when the
signature predates the record). Versions were chosen over timestamps on purpose: two transactions'
`now()` can order differently from their writes under the row lock (a write that began before the
signing and took the lock after it carries an earlier timestamp), while the version compared under the
lock cannot lie. `docs/api/REPORT.md`, "After signing".

### 62.5 What could not be made deterministic, and what was not done

* Which of two simultaneous document registrations wins (item 2) is the unique index's choice:
  a table lock releases both inserts together because their own locks do not conflict. The
  invariant (one 201, one 409 naming it, one row) is asserted order-free; the winner is not.
* Archive versus a `restart` (PR #114) that starts a new execution between the route's `describe`
  and its write: not testable on this branch (the route is not merged here). The compare-and-set on
  `workflow_id` does not cover it (restart keeps the id); the window is a `describe` round trip, the
  consequence is the new execution failing at its first transition on an archived study, and the
  restart route itself takes the row lock and refuses an archived study. Listed as open.
* The web client (`web/`) does not yet read `changed_since_signing` or handle 409 `intake-locked`
  on the intake form; the API answers are documented for it.

### 62.6 Gates

From `backEnd/`: `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy basis`, the catalogue and OpenAPI
`--check` (both regenerated: `BASIS-STUDY-035`, `-031`, the archive and intake descriptions, the
report state and signature members), `evals.freeze_rule_fingerprints --check`,
`tooling/check_no_client_data.py --ci`, pytest `-m "not integration and not slow"` and
`-m "(integration or slow) and not eval_data"`; the results are in the PR. Migration `0027` revises
`0026` (the gate-drafts PR #114, the firm-onboarding PR #111 and the backups PR #115 merged while this
section was written, each with a migration; the migration test's head and history follow them). Error
codes: `025`–`029` are #114's, `030`–`034` the revisions PR's (#117); this section's are `035` and `036`.
Sections 60 and 61 are #115's and #117's; this one was 59, then 60, until they landed.

## 63. Live run 6 on main 15cd291: two studies on the final build, and a lost network window (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Does the build with every pre-firm PR merged (#108 through #119: signing, drafts, firm
onboarding, security, per-user activity, backups and alerts, reopen and revisions, races) still
produce the study live, in both ways an engineer uses it: every gate approved as the model left
it (plain), and the engineer's corrections at every gate (corrected)?

**Setup.** The `basis-web` stack rebuilt from main 15cd291 against the run-5 database copy migrated
0021 to 0027; the same client property, driver `e2e_live3.py`, `--mode plain` then `--mode
corrected`. Private report: `E2E_LIVE_RUN6_2026-11-01.md` in the eval data (the dollars and the
row table). Baselines: run 5 (section 53, plain) and run 3's study A (section 42.5, corrected).

**Results:**

**How to read this table.** Does the final build still produce a correct study live, with and without the engineer's corrections?

- **Models**: the exact model id, its provider, the reasoning effort and the temperature as sent. "temperature default" means the model takes no temperature (reasoning models), so the provider's default applies.
- **Finished; failed steps**: Whether the study finished, and how many workflow steps failed (run 6 plain's 22 failed while the host computer had no network).
- **Processing time** (lower is better): Minutes from start to the finished report, not counting the engineer's time at the reviews.
- **Report lines found (of 38 visible in photos)** (higher is better): How many of the engineer's 38 report lines that photos can show got at least one of our assets.
- **Found lines in the right tax class** (higher is better): Of the lines found, how many land in the engineer's tax class (5, 7, 15 or 39 years).
- **Worst class share error (points)** (lower is better): Largest gap, in percentage points, between our share of dollars and the engineer's in any of the four tax classes.
- **Share in the 39-year class (engineer 80.2 %)**: Share of the study's dollars in the 39-year building class; closer to the engineer's 80.2 % is better.
- **Assets classified from the firm's past rulings** (higher is better): Assets classified by reusing the firm's earlier engineer rulings, with no AI call, out of all assets.
- **Rulings the engineer had to enter** (lower is better): Corrections the engineer had to make at the assets review ('-' = not a corrected study).
- **Study spend (US dollars)** (lower is better): Paid AI and service spend for the study from the call ledger (models, Azure document reading, SAM 3).
- **Tokens (input / output)**: Tokens the run used: input (what the model read) / output (what it wrote; "thinking" is the part spent reasoning, billed as output). "Not recorded" means the run kept no token counts; nothing is estimated.

The Fireplaces row, wrong in run 5 because an approved model answer outranked the engineer's
ruling, is right in both studies: section 54's rule (#109) is confirmed live. The corrected study
needed one ruling (Raised Wood Paneling) where run 3's needed nine, because the database copy
already holds the firm's conventions and #109 serves them first. The one wrong row left in either
study is Access Control, a concealed row the structure model produces (section 44), outside the
evidenced count. The printed report reproduces from the export to the cent in both (87 numbers,
one off by 0.01, as in run 5).

**The 22 failed activities in the plain study are the host's, not Basis's.** `pmset -g log` shows
the Mac running the stack entering sleep at 16:29Z and dark-waking at 16:32Z; in that window the
Docker VM resolved no names (`[Errno -2] Name or service not known` on 17 OpenAI and 3 Anthropic
connections). Two earlier failures were genuine provider timeouts (78 s and 74 s), recovered on
the second attempt. In the no-DNS window seven `analyze_photo` activities exhausted their three
attempts in two seconds and `reconcile_rooms` its three; the workflow flagged the seven photos,
flagged the review that shows the room step's output, and finished with 45 of 52 photos placed
in 43 rooms. That is the designed behaviour (`activity_options.py`: three attempts, one and two
seconds apart, cannot outlast a 20-second outage; a photo's failure never fails the study), and it
is why the plain study lost one evidenced row (Exterior Equipment Concrete Pads, 0.01 % of the
total). The corrected study ran with the host held awake and had no failure.

**Gap found.** The study page says "8 flagged photos. These photos could not be analyzed fully.
They stay visible in the rooms review." The last sentence holds for a photo the model flagged
(it has a room) and not for the seven whose analysis never ran: a photo with no analysis gets no
room (`vision/rooms.py`), the rooms view returns rooms only, and the progress line counts a
flagged photo as analyzed ("52 of 52"). An engineer cannot see which photos were skipped or send
them back for analysis, because only a placed photo carries the re-analyze action. Not a
regression (the behaviour dates from the first live-mode app), but the one item to fix from this
run: the rooms view should return the unplaced photos with their failure code as a section of
their own, with the re-analyze action; the progress line should count completed minus flagged.
Recorded in `web/FRONTEND_BACKLOG.md` section 7. Also observed: `llm_calls` holds 5,683 rows,
every one `status = ok`; a call that times out or fails to connect is never written, so the
ledger can under-count spend during provider trouble (a request the provider completes after the
client gives up is still billed). Low priority.

**Verdict.** No regression on the final build; the corrected study is the best result so far
(35/35, 39-year share within 0.07 points of the engineer's). Spend for the two studies: 5.67.
Open: the unplaced-photos view; failed calls in the ledger; Access Control in the structure model;
a second property, scored blind.

## 64. Every screen of the live app against the final build, with real studies (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Bryan asked that "every page is correct and well tested" and that onboarding "makes
sense". Does each screen of `web/live` load against the API at main 15cd291, show what the API
returns, refuse what it should refuse, and say nothing a customer must not see?

0027), `web/` served from a worktree at 15cd291 on port 3100, the Firebase Auth emulator in
`demo-basis`, the built-in browser pane. Signed in as the firm's owner (the identity the live
driver used, created in the emulator with the same uid) and then as a brand-new account. Data:
the two run-6 studies (plain, 8 flagged photos; corrected, revision 5), the signed run-5 study,
one study waiting at its rooms review. Every API call the pages made was read from the network
log; the browser console and the API log were checked for errors. No model call was made; the
corrected study's revision 5 was signed through the app (no model call).

**What passed** (screen: the API calls behind it):

| screen | result |
|---|---|
| landing, sign-in (`#landing`, `#login`) | loads; emulator sign-in by test account and by Google; copy explains the emulator |
| dashboard, library (`#dashboard`, `#library`) | `GET /v1/me`, `GET /v1/studies?limit=100`; counts, search, status filters, firm switcher; archive via API hides the study |

The API log holds no 5xx and no traceback for the session; the only 4xx are the ones provoked
(400 missing idempotency key, 403 non-operator, 405, 412, 422 x2).

**Defects found.** None in the backend's behaviour. In what the engineer sees:

1. *Flagged photos are invisible on a completed study.* The study page polls the workflow
   view only while processing, so after completion the "8 flagged photos" note and the
   Workflow line are empty; the rooms page lists 43 rooms and 45 of 52 photos with "0 flagged".
   The seven photos of run 6 that were never analyzed appear nowhere. Backend side fixed here:

   revision holds, each with `analyzed` (false: the analysis never produced a result), the same
   list on every page (`OutputRepository.unplaced_photos`; `tests/api/test_outputs.py`: two
   unplaced photos at the current revision, one analyzed and one not; all five at revision 1;
   every page carries the list). Frontend side: FRONTEND_BACKLOG 7 and 8.
2. *Live mode shows mock data on two screens.* The Activity page renders the design mock's
   invented feed ("Illustrative events") and never calls `GET /v1/me/activity` (which answers
   with the real events); Settings shows the mock user, mock firm and a "preview" cost source.
   A signed-in engineer would take both for real. FRONTEND_BACKLOG 8.
3. *Provider and layer names reach the engineer* (the rule of 2026-11-01): the photo viewer
   prints "SAM 3 · 11 counted instances · model 1bf97763"; the assets table and asset page print
   the method token (`cache · 1250`, `rule`, `llm`, `manual`). FRONTEND_BACKLOG 8.
4. *Stale copy*: Team said "No email is sent" (invitations are emailed since #111); fixed here
   (`web/live/live-team.js`). The preview header says "Local PDF · not uploaded". FRONTEND_BACKLOG 8.
5. *Broken image*: `assets/kitchen.webp` (the landing hero preview) is not in the repo; two

6. *Docs vs repo*: `docs/api/OPS_HEALTH.md` pointed at a developer page `web/developer/` that

**Observations, not defects.**

- Every appraisal field shows "Low confidence": the grounded extraction gives every accepted
  model value the constant 0.6 by design (`extraction/grounded.py`: self-reported confidence is
  not calibrated), so the badge says nothing. The honest label is the source ("read by the
  model; verify on p. 3"). Design item for the appraisal screen.
- The classifier names an unmatched component's category "Unclassified: <label>" and the
  schedule prints it; wording for the router.
- Two member rows of the firm share one email (two emulator uids). Expected with the emulator;
  a rule of one membership per verified email per firm is worth adding before firms sign in
  with Google.
- Not in the live app at all, each with its API ready: revisions and reopen, study audit and
  timeline, per-user activity, cost indices, retention, reprice, spend, the result worksheet,

**Verdict.** The backend behaves as its contracts say on every screen and every write is
conditional and refused correctly; the app renders the real data on the study screens and the
report flow end to end, including signing. What fails is honesty at the edges: two screens
show mock data in live mode, flagged photos have no home, and three places name the layers.
None of it is a backend defect; the one backend gap (the rooms view hiding unplaced photos) is
closed in this section's PR.


## 65. Browser error capture: every error a user hits, recorded in detail and diagnosable from the record (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Bryan asked that every error a user hits be saved "in extreme detail (firm, user,
page, action, time, everything) whenever they occur on a user end so we can work on fixing those
bugs whenever they occur". Before this section the API logged its own failures with a request id,
and the browser showed a toast with the message and the request id; what the user did before, on
which screen, in which build and browser, and the errors that never reached the API (an uncaught
exception, a rejected promise, a resource that failed to load) were lost when the tab closed. This
section designs the capture against how the established tools do it, builds the browser module,
the ingest route, the store, the timeline link, the operator reads and the operator page, tests
every path, and proves it on a live stack by breaking the page on purpose. Contract:
docs/api/CLIENT_ERRORS.md; code: `web/live/errors.js`, `basis/api/routes/client_errors.py`,
migration `0028_client_errors`, `web/developer/client-errors.html`.

### 65.1 The standard: Sentry, OpenTelemetry, Google Cloud Error Reporting

Read before designing (the pages are linked from the design's docstrings and the contract):

| Source | What it names | Taken |
|---|---|---|
| Sentry event payload (`develop.sentry.dev/sdk/.../event-payloads`) | required `event_id` (a UUID the SDK mints), `timestamp`, `platform`; optional `level` (fatal/error/warning/info/debug, default error), `logger`, `transaction` (the route), `release` (a git sha), `environment`, `tags`, `extra`, `fingerprint`; interfaces `exception` (type, value, stacktrace with frames: filename, function, lineno, colno), `breadcrumbs` (timestamp, type, category, message, data), `user` (id, email, ip), `request` (method, url, headers with bodies capped at 8 kB), `contexts` (browser, os, device; each capped at 8 kB), `sdk` | `event_id`, `occurred_at`, `level`, the exception's type/message/stack/source, `breadcrumbs`, `user`, `build` as the release, `http` as the request, `client` as the contexts, `capture_version` as the sdk |
| Sentry browser SDK options (`docs.sentry.io/platforms/javascript/configuration/options`) and Dedupe integration | `maxBreadcrumbs` default 100; `sampleRate` 1.0; `normalizeDepth` 3; `attachStacktrace`; `beforeSend`/`beforeBreadcrumb` to scrub; a `fetch` transport by default, dropping events when offline; Dedupe (on by default) drops an event identical to the previous one by stack and fingerprint; client reports count dropped events by reason | 50 breadcrumbs (a Basis session is short and an event is at most about 40 KB), depth 3 for context, dedupe within 5 s with `repeats`, `dropped` counted per cap; no sampling: every error is wanted |
| OpenTelemetry exception semantic conventions (logs) and browser/user-agent attributes | `exception.type` (dynamic class name), `exception.message` (may hold sensitive data), `exception.stacktrace` (the runtime's natural string); record handled exceptions at WARN and unhandled at ERROR; `browser.language` from `navigator.language`, `browser.platform` from `userAgentData.platform` (else unset), `browser.mobile`, `user_agent.original`; `http.request.method`, `http.response.status_code`; the log data model's `Timestamp` (when it happened) beside `ObservedTimestamp` (when it was collected) | `error_type`/`message`/`stack`; `level` warning for a 4xx and error for a 5xx or no response; `client.language`/`platform`/`user_agent`; `http.method`/`status`; `occurred_at` (the browser) beside `received_at` (the database) with `clock_offset_ms` between them |
| Google Cloud Error Reporting (`ReportedErrorEvent`, "formatting error messages") | `eventTime`, `serviceContext` {service, version}, `message` with a stack trace or `context.reportLocation` {filePath, lineNumber, functionName}, `context.httpRequest` {method, url, userAgent, referrer, responseStatusCode, remoteIp}, `context.user`; grouped by stack | `source` {file, line, column, function} when the stack is empty (a resource failure, a cross-origin `Script error.`), `build.api_git_sha` as the version, `_server.remote_addr`; the API's own log lines already carry `stack_trace` and are what Error Reporting would group |

What Basis adds that none of them has, because Basis has it: the firm (`org_id`), the study with
its revision and stage, the screen (the hash route and the app's screen name), the gate decision
breadcrumbs, the problem's catalogue `code` and `request_id` on a failed call (so the browser's
record and the server's log line meet on one id), the attempt under the idempotency key (a retry
is not a new error), and the field names of a request body (never the values: the intake and the
corrections are client data).

### 65.2 Design against the seams we have

* **The browser** (`web/live/errors.js`, loaded first on `index.html`, 290 lines, no
  dependencies at install): hooks `window` `error` (exceptions and resource failures),
  `unhandledrejection`, `console.error`, the API client's new `observe` hook (every request:
  method, path, status, duration, request id, code, attempt, body object), `Basis.reportError`;
  breadcrumbs for `data-live`/`data-action` clicks, hash navigation, every API call, gate
  decisions (`live-review.js`), console errors. The live app passes the hook to `createClient`,
  reports a failed action (`guarded`) and a failed loader that was not an API refusal, and exposes
  `Live.screen()`. Context is read lazily from `BasisAuth.user`, `BasisLive.firm()` and
  `BasisLive.state`, so the module needs nothing at load and an error before sign-in still
  records the page.
* **Transport:** `fetch` with `keepalive: true` (survives unload; `sendBeacon` cannot carry the
  bearer token, and the route is authenticated like every other), batches of 20 at most once
  every 5 s, one `Idempotency-Key` per batch kept across retries (429/5xx/no response: 2 s, 8 s,
  32 s, then dropped; any other 4xx dropped at once), a queue of 50, 30 events a minute (`dropped`
  counts the rest on the next event), identical errors within 5 s folded (`repeats`), flush on
  `pagehide` and `visibilitychange: hidden`, events queued while nobody is signed in and sent after
  sign-in. The module's own route and its own console use cannot produce an event.
* **Redaction** on the client and again on the server: ids in paths and routes become `{id}`
  (UUIDs, long hex, long numbers), query values go (`?limit=…`), `Bearer …` and JWT-shaped strings
  are masked in free text, a request body is reduced to its field names, any key matching the
  logging redaction pattern (key, token, secret, password, authorization; the client adds cookie
  and session) is `***` to depth 3; strings are bounded (message 4,000, stack 16,000, others 500);
  the server masks the whole event with `basis.obs.logging.redact` before storing. NUL is refused
  (PostgreSQL text), so no event can turn into a 500.
* **The route** `POST /v1/client-errors` is a `write_router` route (token, any firm role, a user
  with no firm too, the mutation rate limit, the idempotency key the contract test requires on
  every POST), with its own 256 KiB cap checked in a dependency before the body is parsed (413
  `BASIS-API-045`; a junk body over the cap is 413, under it 422) and 30 batches a minute per
  user. 202 with `stored`/`duplicates`/`ids`.
* **Verified, not trusted:** the reporter is the token's user; `org_id` is set only when the
  reporter belongs to the claimed firm (or to exactly one firm when none is claimed); `study_id`
  only when `StudyRepository.get_visible` says the reporter can see it. The claims stay inside the
  event with `_server.org_verified`/`study_visible`. So a browser cannot write a timeline row into
  another firm's study (the tenancy rule of `test_tenancy.py`, kept).
* **The timeline:** an event on a visible study appends `client.error` in the same transaction
  (`StudyEventRepository.record`: actor engineer, `request_id` from the logging context, `code`,
  `entity_type` `client_error`, `entity_id` the record, `stage`/`revision` the row's, the claim in
  `detail`). It shows in `GET .../timeline` and `GET /v1/me/activity`; the audit lists engineer
  actions and an error is not one, so it is unchanged.
* **The store:** `client_errors` (migration 0028): `seq` identity for the keyset cursor, the
  client's `event_id` unique (`INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, so a retried batch stores each
  event once), the filter columns indexed by (`org_id`, `seq`), (`user_id`, `seq`), (`study_id`,
  `seq`), `code`, `request_id`, `created_at`; `event` JSONB with `_server` {received_at, sent_at,
  clock_offset_ms, api_request_id, api_git_sha, api_env, reporter, org_verified, study_visible,
  remote_addr}; `forbid_mutation()` on UPDATE (the `takeoffs` rule); deleted only by the purge.
* **Operators:** `GET /v1/ops/client-errors` (filters org, user, study, code, kind, request id,
  since/until on the time received; newest first; cursor) and `GET .../{id}` (the whole event),
  behind the same allowlist as `GET /v1/ops/health` (`require_operator`, moved to
  `basis/api/operators.py` because a route module importing `routes.ops` imports `api.health`,
  which imports the routes package: a cycle). `web/developer/client-errors.html` (with
  `client-errors-model.js`, node-tested) is the list with the filters and a detail view of every
  fact, the stack, the context, the last actions and the whole event; it signs in with the app's
  Firebase session through the app's API client.
* **Retention:** a fixed `CLIENT_ERRORS_RETENTION_DAYS` (180), `python -m basis.retention
  purge-client-errors` (dry run counts; batches of 1,000), not the firm's rule: the records are
  operational data about the application that name a user, a firm and a study id, never a
  document or a price; the firm's rule purges a study's uploads; a bug reported a quarter late
  still needs its record (Sentry keeps 90 days). The `client.error` timeline rows stay.
* **Correlation on the server** (the gaps the task asked to fill): the verified `uid` is bound
  into the logging context by `get_optional_principal`, the database `user_id` by
  `get_current_user`, `study_id`/`org_id`/`role` by `require_study_access` and
  `require_org_role`; every problem's log line and the unhandled-exception line carry the matched
  `route` template, `status`, `error_code`, the exception's type and message (a 5xx problem logs
  at WARNING); the worker's activity interceptor binds `study_id` and writes one `activity failed`
  line at ERROR with the code, the exception type and the traceback (the SDK's own failure log
  runs after the interceptor returns, outside the bound context). So `event.http.request_id`
  finds one server line with everything about the request that failed.

### 65.3 What a stored event holds

The uncaught `TypeError` from the live check (65.5), as `GET /v1/ops/client-errors/{id}`
returned it (ids shortened):

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| columns | `kind` error, `error_type` TypeError, `message` "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'rooms')", `occurred_at` (browser) and `received_at` (database), `user_id`, `org_id` (verified), `study_id` (visible), `revision` 1, `stage` uploading, `route` `#processing/{id}`, `screen` processing, `code` null, `http_status` null, `request_id` null, `build_sha` `15cd291-dirty`, `web_version` `live-16`, `user_agent` |
| `event.source` / `stack` | `{file, line 5, column 49, function}`; the stack as the browser gave it |
| `event.user` / `firm` / `study` / `page` | uid, email, role owner; the firm's id and name; study id, revision, stage, status; hash route, screen, path |
| `event.breadcrumbs` (10) | `load #login` → click Sign in → `GET /v1/me → 0` (the CORS failure of the first attempt, 8 ms) → click reload-me → `GET /v1/me → 200` (134 ms, request id) → `GET /v1/studies?limit=… → 200` → `#dashboard → #processing/{id}` → `GET /v1/studies/{id} → 200` → `POST /v1/studies/{id}/start → 422 BASIS-STUDY-001` (57 ms, request id) → the console error, each with the client's clock and `since_load_ms` |
| `event.client` | user agent, platform macOS, en-US, viewport 1024×768 @2x, online, time zone, connection 4g, visible, cookies |
| `event.build` | API git sha from `/health`, web asset version |
| `event._server` | received_at, sent_at, clock_offset_ms, the report's own request id, the API's sha and env, the reporter's uid and user id, `org_verified` true, `study_visible` true, remote address |
| timeline | `client.error`, actor engineer, `entity_id` the record, `request_id` the report's, `detail` kind/message/screen/route/http/build/event id; listed under `GET /v1/me/activity` |
| API log | `client error recorded` with `error_code BASIS-CLIENT-001`, `client_error_id`, `kind`, `client_code`, `client_request_id`, `uid`, `user_id`, `request_id`; and for the failed start, the `problem` line with `request_id f6b17ca4…`, `uid`, `user_id`, `study_id`, `org_id`, `role owner`, `route /v1/studies/{study_id}/start`, `status 422`, `error_code BASIS-STUDY-001` |

The `api` event for the failed start additionally holds `http`: method, route, status 422, code
`BASIS-STUDY-001`, the request id, the problem type, title and detail, latency 57 ms, attempt 1,
`body_fields` null; the `report` event holds the context with `apiKey` masked to `***` and `note`
kept.

### 65.4 Tests

| Suite | Count | What it protects |
|---|---|---|
| `web/tests/errors.test.cjs` (node) | 17 | redaction (ids, query values, bearer and JWT text, body field names, secret keys, NUL); stack parsing (V8, Firefox, bare); every field of an event; the API build read once and filled in; each kind; the `observe` hook (attempt under the key, no token, a broken observer never breaks a request); breadcrumbs (click, navigation, decision; ring of 50); dedupe with `repeats`; 30 a minute with `dropped`; a throwing render loop sends one batch of at most 20; batching with the bearer token, keepalive and the key kept across retries; three retries then dropped; a 4xx dropped at once; queued without a token and sent after sign-in; mock mode sends nothing; flush on hide without retry; a broken context getter and a logging listener cannot recurse; the client clock stamp is the same instant as `Date.now()` (added after the live check, 65.5); the sample fixture is what the module produces |
| `web/tests/client-errors-page.test.cjs` (node) | 6 | the operator page's query, rows, issues table, status form, the copy brief, detail and tree, escaped |
| `tests/api/test_client_errors.py` (integration) | 41 (14 parametrized malformed bodies, 8 bad parameters) | the sample fixture is accepted (client shape = server schema); every detail stored and the timeline row with provenance, the activity listing, the audit unchanged; a viewer posts and gets their one firm; claims the reporter cannot make stay inside the event with no timeline row; no study, no row; a non-catalogue code not indexed; one store per `event_id` across batches and a replay; secrets masked anywhere; 422 naming the field; 413 before validation and 422 under the cap; 429 after 30 batches, per user; 401 without a token, 202 without a firm; operators list newest first with every filter and a cursor, 422 for bad parameters, read one record with `_server`, 404 unknown; a firm owner is 403 `not-operator`; the correlation log lines (unhandled exception: request id, uid, user id, route, status, exception type and message, stack trace, ERROR; a study problem: study id, firm, role, route, code; a 404: study id only; the recorded line); the schema's kinds are the table's |
| `tests/integration/db/test_client_error_records.py` | 9 | the repository's insert once per `event_id`, the never-updated trigger, the check constraints, listing with every filter and the cursor, the purge in batches with a dry run, `cutoff_for`, the CLI's summary line and arguments |
| `tests/unit/worker/test_worker_parts.py` | +1 | a failed activity's one ERROR line with the study, the code, the exception type and message and the traceback, the context unbound afterwards |
| `tests/unit/config/test_settings.py` | +1 | `CLIENT_ERRORS_RETENTION_DAYS` default 180, 1 to 3650 |
| existing walks | | `test_health.py` known routes (+3), `test_auth.py` (401 on all three), `test_openapi_contract.py` (Schemathesis on all three; the idempotency key required on the POST), `test_models_metadata.py` (`client_errors` columns, the no-update tables), `test_migrations.py` (head 0028, 28 revisions, downgrade and up) |

Mutation checks done while writing: the clock stamp test fails against the first `stamp()`
(65.5); the dedupe test fails with `dedupeMs: 0`; the 413 test fails with the size dependency
removed (the junk body becomes 422); the claims test fails with `get_visible` replaced by `get`
(the other firm's study gets a timeline row); the correlation test fails without the `bind`
calls (no `uid`, no `study_id` on the lines).

### 65.5 The live check

A stack built from this branch: Postgres in its own container (`client-errors-pg`, port 55433),
migrations to 0028, the API on port 8200 with `BASIS_ENV=dev`, the Auth emulator the walkthrough
session already ran, `OPS_OPERATOR_UIDS` set to a test account created in the emulator for this
check, the web app served from this worktree on port 3300; nothing paid, the Docker stack of the
walkthrough session untouched. Then, signed in as that account in a firm created by the admin
CLI, on the processing screen of a draft study: `POST .../start` (422 `intake-required`), a
`console.error` with a `RangeError`, an unhandled rejection, `Basis.reportError` with a context
holding `apiKey`, and an uncaught `TypeError` from a timer; before that, the first sign-in had hit
a CORS failure (the API started with the wrong origin), which the module recorded as a `status 0`
event and delivered after three retries once the API was restarted.

Results: 6 records stored, one batch of 5 plus the retried one; every column and every member of
65.3 filled; the five study events on the study's timeline and under `/me/activity`; the API log
lines with `BASIS-CLIENT-001`; the operator page lists them with the filters and the detail shows
every fact, the stack, the ten breadcrumbs and the whole event (screenshots in the session). Two
defects found by the check and fixed before the PR, neither visible to the unit tests because
their expected values came from the code:

1. **The client clock was 7 hours off.** `occurred_at` was the UTC time with the local offset
   appended (`00:19:49-07:00` for an event at `00:19:49Z`), so `clock_offset_ms` read 25,199,976.
   Fixed to shift the time into the zone; a node test now asserts `Date.parse(occurred_at)`
   equals the fake clock. Verified live after the fix: `2026-11-01T17:21:50.223-07:00` for a
   record received at `00:21:50Z`, offset under a second.
2. **`screen` was null.** The module read `window.state.screen`, but the design's `state` is a
   script-scoped binding, not a window property. The live app now exposes `Live.screen()`.
   Verified live: `processing`.

Found in passing, not this change's: `POST /v1/orgs` answers 500 whenever the API log level
is INFO, because `routes/orgs.py` logs `extra={"name": ...}` and `name` is a reserved
`LogRecord` attribute (`KeyError: Attempt to overwrite 'name'`); the test suite runs at WARNING,
so it never saw it. The new correlation line showed it at once (`exception_type=KeyError`,
`route=/v1/orgs`, the uid and user id). Reported to Bryan as a one-line follow-up.

### 65.6 Limits (what cannot be captured)

Cross-origin scripts report `Script error.` without a stack (the Firebase SDK on `gstatic.com`
is one; the page, user and breadcrumbs still come through); a tab crash or a navigation before
the keepalive request leaves may lose the last batch (browsers cap keepalive bodies at 64 KB in
flight per origin); an error before the module loads, and errors while signed out that are never
followed by a sign-in on that page, are lost; the text a user typed is never recorded, by design;
if the app ever ships minified, stacks need source maps; events beyond the caps are counted, not
kept; the server's own view is not copied into the record but found by the request id in the API
and worker logs, which have their own retention.

### 65.7 Issues, status and the copy brief (added the same day)

Bryan's follow-up: a record should be copyable into a coding agent's prompt in one go, and a
developer should be able to mark a bug resolved, in progress or still open; he expected the
status to be manual and asked whether anything could be automatic. The answer, from how
Sentry and every tracker do it: the status is a person's call, but two things are not.
Records are grouped into **issues** by a fingerprint (kind, error type, the message with
numbers and ids normalized, the top frame's file and function, the route and status of a
failed call: the same bug on two firms is one issue, a different frame is another), and the
ingest keeps each issue's `occurrences`, `first_seen_at`, `last_seen_at` and `last_build_sha`.
The status (`open` on first sight, then `in_progress`, `resolved`, `ignored`, set by an
operator with a note, who and when) records `status_build_sha`, the build the issue had last
been seen on; the one automatic transition is `resolved` -> `regressed` when a new
occurrence arrives on a different build (same build: the fix is not deployed yet, the issue
stays resolved and the count moves). Nothing can detect that a bug is fixed; the system can
detect that it came back, and that is what it automates (Sentry's "resolved in the next
release" and regression rule).

Built: `client_error_issues` (in migration 0028, with `set_updated_at()`),
`client_errors.fingerprint`, the upsert in `ClientErrorRepository.record` (a duplicate event
id counts nothing), `GET /v1/ops/client-errors/issues[/{fingerprint}]`,
`PUT .../issues/{fingerprint}/status`, `status`/`fingerprint` filters and `issue_status` on
the records, the issues table and status controls on the developer page, and **Copy for an
agent**: one plain-text brief with every fact of the record (both clocks and the offset,
user, firm, study, screen, request with its code and request id, source, build, browser,
stack, context, the breadcrumbs with their times) and where to look next (the server log
line by request id, the record's URL, the study's timeline, the contract), plus **Copy
JSON**. Tests: three API tests (one issue across users and firms with its counts and build;
a person's status with who/when/build, the regression on another build and not on the same,
the records filtered by status, every refusal; the issues page with its cursor), two
repository tests (the fingerprint names the bug not the occurrence; the counts, the duplicate,
the regression rule, the cursor), two node tests (the issues table and status form; the
brief's every line and its plain-text form). Verified live on the stack of 65.5 after the
change (the database rebuilt at the final 0028, which also caught a foreign key the first
draft of the migration lacked; `alembic check` and the up/down/up of `test_migrations.py`
pass on it): the same uncaught `TypeError` raised twice was one issue with count 2 beside
the 422 start and a report; `resolved` with a note set from the page recorded who, when and
the build; the same error re-posted with another build sha turned the issue `regressed`
with count 3 and `last_build_sha` the new build; the brief came back as one plain-text block
with every fact, the stack, the four breadcrumbs and the four places to look next.
