## 66. `POST /v1/orgs` answered 500 at `LOG_LEVEL=INFO`: a reserved `extra=` key, and a guard for the class (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Found during the browser error capture work (section 65.5): every deployed stack
runs the API at `LOG_LEVEL=INFO`, and there creating a firm answered an opaque 500
(`BASIS-API-024`). Why, why did no test see it, and how is the next one caught?

**Standard.** The stdlib documents that the keys passed in `extra` must not clash with the
logging system's own; `logging.Logger.makeRecord` enforces it by raising
`KeyError("Attempt to overwrite %r in LogRecord")` for `message`, `asctime` and any attribute
the record already carries (`name`, `msg`, `args`, `module`, `lineno`, `taskName`...). The
established check is the flake8-logging-format rule G101 (`logging-extra-attr-clash`), which
ruff implements; this repository did not select it (`select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]`).
G101 finds loggers by a name heuristic (`logging.*`, names starting `log` or ending `logger`
defined in the same file) plus the `logger-objects` setting.

**The bug.** `api/routes/orgs.py` logged `firm created` and `firm renamed` with
`extra={..., "name": org.name}`. `name` is the logger's name on every record, so building the
record raised, the exception left the route, and the request answered 500. Both routes: the
rename was broken the same way. The request's transaction rolls back on an exception
(`db/session.py` `session_scope`), and a probe on the old code confirmed it: after the 500 the
database held 0 firms, 0 members and 0 firm events, so a retry was safe and nothing needs
cleaning up.

**Why the suite missed it.** A record is built only when its level is enabled. The test suite's
root logger sits at WARNING, so `logger.info(...)` returned before `makeRecord`, and the 64
tests in `test_firms.py` that create and rename firms all passed. The health tests install the
Basis handler at DEBUG (`log_stream`), but only around `/health`.

**Fix.** The key is `firm_name` in both calls (`docs/api/FIRMS.md` lists it). Neither check
below finds another collision in the backend.

**Measured: G101 against an `ast` walk.** A scratch copy of `basis/` with a `"name"` key
inserted into every one of the 61 `extra={...}` literals on a logger method (a 62nd `extra=`
is not a literal):

| Check | Injected keys caught | Misses |
|---|---|---|
| G101, default settings | 53 / 61 | all 8 `workflow.logger.*` calls in `workflow/study_workflow.py` (an imported logger; a raise there fails the workflow task, not one request) |
| G101 with `logger-objects = ["temporalio.workflow.logger", "temporalio.activity.logger"]` | 61 / 61 | a reserved key reached through `{**fields}` or `extra=fields` (synthetic source: neither flagged) |
| the `ast` walk (`test_log_extra_keys.py`) | 61 / 61 | nothing in the synthetic cases; an `extra=` it cannot read is listed by hand |

**Guard.** Both, since each covers what the other does not:

* G101 is selected in `backEnd/pyproject.toml` with the two Temporal loggers named. It runs in
  the editor, the pre-commit hook (ruff v0.17.0, the locked version, reading the same file)
  and CI's `ruff check .`, over `basis/`, `tests/` and `evals/`.
* `tests/unit/obs/test_log_extra_keys.py`, no database: walks every `basis/**/*.py` with `ast`,
  finds each `extra=` on a logger method (`debug` ... `critical`, `exception`, `log`, on any
  receiver), and checks its keys against the running interpreter's reserved set (the record's
  attributes plus `message` and `asctime`, the exact `makeRecord` test, verified key by key).
  It reads `{...}` and `dict(...)`, and follows a `**spread` or bare name whose source is a
  mapping assigned once in the same function, which resolves every relay call. Of the 62
  calls, one is not readable (`retrieval/ingest.py` `write_prepared`,
  `IngestResult.summary()`, whose eleven keys were read by hand); it is listed, and any new
  unreadable `extra=` fails until it is read and listed too. 8 tests.
* `tests/api/test_firm_logging.py`, `integration`: the real routes with the Basis handler on
  the root logger at DEBUG. `POST /v1/orgs` answers 201 and its log line carries `firm_name`;
  `PATCH /v1/orgs/{id}` on a seeded firm (so it fails on the rename alone) answers 200. 2 tests.

**Proof.** Against main ac24943 (the old `orgs.py`): `ruff check .` reports G101 at
`orgs.py:131` and `:150`; both API tests answer 500 with
`KeyError: "Attempt to overwrite 'name' in LogRecord"`; the walk names `api/routes/orgs.py:130`
and `:149` (the call's line). With the fix: ruff clean, 10 of 10 pass; `test_firms.py`,
`test_health.py` and `tests/unit/obs` 149 passed before the last test was added; unit suite
unit suite 4851 passed, 10 skipped (private eval data), 0 failed in 87 s; format, mypy, catalogue, OpenAPI, rule fingerprints and the client-data guard
green; provider keys unset.

**Not covered.** The walk reads `basis/` only (G101 covers the literals in `tests/` and
`evals/`); an `extra=` built in another function and passed in is listed by hand, not
checked. The suite still runs at WARNING: raising the whole suite to INFO would catch more
than this class, but changes every test's captured output and is left as a separate decision.

## 70. Completion requires the current signed report (2026-11-01)

**Correction to section 68.** A backend `completed` study has finished its review
workflow; it may still have an unsigned report or inputs changed after signing.
Calling that study completed was premature. The user requires completed to mean
approved, signed, current and ready to deliver.

**Standard.** Docusign distinguishes individual signing from overall completion:
https://www.docusign.com/blog/developers/dsdev-has-my-envelope-been-signed.
The existing Basis report contract (`docs/api/REPORT.md`, `ReportStateOut` and
`GET .../report/state`) provides the current revision, export/skip state, missing
inputs, signature and input changes since signing. The UI uses that evidence;
it does not infer a signature from the workflow status or create a new backend
stage.

**Change.** Report & sign is now a separate final navigation step after Results,
with the existing details forms, preview, signing controls and downloads. A
study is displayed as completed only when the backend reviews are complete,
report and signature match the study and revision, export is present and not
skipped, no required inputs are missing, and tracked changes since signing are
explicitly empty. Unsigned, outdated, unknown, unavailable and loading states
cannot receive the green completed banner. Closed reviews retain a separate
Read-only review label. Results and progress use the same status above their
navigation; progress remains at six of seven steps until the final check passes.
Report evidence is cached by revision and refreshed when entering study screens.
Home/Library describe the backend-only status as Reviews approved.

Signed report instructions no longer ask the user to sign again or say an
outdated PDF is the one to deliver. The old signed PDF remains downloadable and
immutable. Touch targets in the final report are at least 44 px, checklist rows
wrap on narrow screens, and navigation keeps the selected step visible after a
resize. Custom live routes now receive the screen attribute used by their styles.

**Measured.** 295/295 frontend tests pass. Added completion cases cover missing
signature/details, changed firm/study/both, untracked changes, unexported/skipped
reports, missing checklist, mismatched study/revision, pending/error/missing
responses and non-completed workflow states. Existing gates and legacy studies
retain their review access. Controller tests verify the dedicated final route,
no writes on render, correct study/revision cache keys, signed downloads and
retained preview/sign handlers. Existing signing tests retain ETag, permission,
input and signature guards.

Browser checks verified an existing unsigned local study and the signed study
with changed inputs from the user's screenshot. The latter now shows Report
needs updating and six of seven steps complete. No warnings/errors were recorded
in the live review tab. The isolated report-completion fixture verifies awaiting
signature, signed/current, untracked signature and failed status loading without
live API calls. At 320 and 390 CSS px it measures page width equal to viewport
width and report/navigation controls of at least 44 px. The selected final step,
wrapped checklist and lower downloads were visually inspected.

**Limits.** No backend state or signing contract changed. No live signature,
report input save, study write, paid provider request, deployment or merge was
performed. The green completion screenshot is explicitly synthetic; it does
not attest or sign an existing study. Revision creation and re-signing remain
subject to the existing backend workflow. Screenshots are outside the repository.

The signature checklist also distinguishes the next action (preview, then sign) from an already recorded signature; both wording branches are asserted in `web/tests/report.test.cjs`.

## 72. Report & sign verified end to end: the live stack, the recovery path, the gaps (2026-11-01)

**Question.** Does "Study completed" hold only when every review is approved *and* the current
revision's report is exported, signed for this study and revision, lacks no required input and
has no change since signing (sections 70 and 71 made that the rule in the web app); and does the
whole step work against the real API, worker and storage, including after the inputs change
following a signature?

**Standard.** DocuSign's guidance separates "a recipient signed" from "the envelope is
completed" and reads completion from the authoritative envelope status, never from the client
action (https://www.docusign.com/blog/developers/dsdev-has-my-envelope-been-signed). ESIGN/UETA
elements and what the Basis signature is and is not: STUDY_REPORT_SPEC 11.13. The append-only
revision model (git revert, Wikipedia undo): REVISIONS.md section 1. The web app's completion
rule reads `GET .../report/state` (REPORT.md "Signing", "After signing") and nothing else.

**Setup (all isolated, nothing shared with the `basis-web` stack or any client file).** The
tree is main ac24943 with PR #122, the Codex `codex/frontend-primary` working tree (committed
verbatim, its sections renumbered 67-71 because #123 is 65 and #124 is 66), PR #123 and
PR #124 merged. A fresh Postgres (`pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, container `report-sign-pg`,
port 55434, migrated to 0028), a Temporal dev server on 7434, the API on 8400
(`BASIS_ENV=dev`, `TMPDIR` under the session scratchpad so `LOCAL_STORAGE_DIR` is its own),
the outbox relay, a worker on the API's task queue built from the lifecycle suite's offline
providers (`FixtureVisionProvider`, `FixtureAzureDi`, the scripted classifier, the published
test reference corpus: no provider key in the process, no paid call possible), the web app
from this worktree on 3400, and the Firebase Auth emulator already running on 9099 (two new
accounts, `report-sign-owner` and `report-sign-viewer`, in the demo project). Studies are the
lifecycle suite's synthetic study (the synthetic URAR appraisal, three fixture photos), started
and approved through the real API and relay. One synthetic 2025 historical cost index row was
entered with the refresh CLI (`source manual`, citation says it is synthetic); the first study
(purchase price 650,000) withheld its allocation at reconciliation (+36.8 % against RCNLD,
outside 10 %) and its export skipped the report (`BASIS-REPORT-002`), which became the
"skipped" case below; the study used for signing was priced at 445,000 (gap 0.3 %) and
exported a report (11 pages, DRAFT watermark, Exhibits A-C).

### 72.2 The recovery path after a signature, exercised live

After signing, the study details were edited in the app: banner "Report needs updating ·
Details changed after signing. The previous signed PDF is preserved; an updated revision must
be reviewed and signed before delivery", step "Update required", badge "Signed earlier",
`changed_since_signing` `["study"]`. **There was no way to make that revision in the app**: a
dead end (the wording was right, the action missing). The documented path is a reopen at the
assets review (REVISIONS.md section 2: the approved assets carried, only the export reruns, the
new report carries the stored inputs). Added to the step, for engineers and owners of a
`completed` study with a signature: "Start a new revision" reads the plan (`POST .../reopen`
with `dry_run`), shows it ("Revision 2 opens at the assets review with the assets of revision 1
as they were approved… The signed report of revision 1 is kept"), and on confirmation reopens.

Live: 202, the progress page followed the new execution ("Assets review is ready", "4 of 7
complete", revision 2; timeline `stage.entered`, `study.reopened`, `run.started`,
`revision.carried` with 18 assets, 10 components, 2 rooms, `gate.opened`), the assets review
showed the 18 carried assets ($410,483) and was approved in the app (decision through the
relay), the export ran (the Results page landed on does not poll: FRONTEND_BACKLOG 9), and
Report & sign read revision 2: "Awaiting signature", badge Draft, Sign disabled until the
preview, and a new section "Earlier signed reports · Revision 1 · signed Nov 1, 8:50 PM" with
its own download (`GET .../report?format=pdf&revision=1`, from `GET .../revisions`). Preview
and sign: "Study completed · Revision 2 is approved and signed…".

**How to read this table.** After a signed report is reopened and signed again, is each signed version kept intact?

- **Models**: the exact model id, its provider, the reasoning effort and the temperature as sent. "temperature default" means the model takes no temperature (reasoning models), so the provider's default applies.
- **Signature record**: The stored signature: the file's fingerprint (sha256) and the record's version numbers.
- **Signing events on the timeline**: Signing events recorded, and whether they carry the same file fingerprint.
- **Signed files stored**: Signed PDFs kept for the revision (1 expected).
- **Download of that revision's report**: What the report download returns for that revision.
- **What the revisions list says**: How the revisions list describes it: how it began, exported, signed, current or not.
- **Tokens (input / output)**: Tokens the run used: input (what the model read) / output (what it wrote; "thinking" is the part spent reasoning, billed as output). "Not recorded" means the run kept no token counts; nothing is estimated.

| Report revision | Models (provider, effort, temperature) | Signature record | Signing events on the timeline | Signed files stored | Download of that revision's report | What the revisions list says | Tokens (input / output) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rev 1 · The original signed report, kept and still downloadable | No AI model | sha256 `6f4f64c6…`, versions 1 / 2 | 1, same sha256 | 1 | `…-rev-1-report-signed.pdf`, bytes identical to the download taken before the reopen | origin start, exported, signed, not current | None (offline test fixtures stand in for every AI call) |
| rev 2 · Reopened at the assets review after a change, approved and signed again | No AI model | sha256 `234b8bba…`, versions 1 / 3 | 1, same sha256 | 1 | `…-rev-2-report-signed.pdf` (the default) | origin reopen, exported, signed, current | None (offline test fixtures stand in for every AI call) |

### 72.3 Defects found and fixed (each with a test)

1. **Dead end after a changed signature** (72.2): the Report & sign step now offers the new
   revision and lists earlier signed PDFs (`web/live/live-report.js`; `web/tests/
   primary-frontend.test.cjs`: the control appears for engineers and owners of a completed
   signed study only, the dry run is read first and the reopen happens only on confirmation,
   earlier signed revisions are listed by number with the current one and unsigned ones left
   out, a failed history says so without hiding the report). REPORT.md "After signing" names
   the path.
2. **A refusal the client expects was a client error**: the firm profile's 404 before the
   owner saves it was captured as a warning on every load of the step (two records in the
   walkthrough). `api.request(path, {expect: [404]})` marks it; the capture keeps the
   breadcrumb and files no event (`web/live/api-client.js`, `web/live/errors.js`;
   `web/tests/errors.test.cjs`).
3. **The merged tree threw on any failed action in a harness**: `guarded` and `load` tested
   `e instanceof BasisApi.ApiError`, and the Codex test harness and the synthetic fixture stub
   `BasisApi` without it (`TypeError: Right-hand side of 'instanceof' is not an object`, one web
   test failing after the merge). `apiRefusal()` checks the class exists first
   (`web/live/live-app.js`).
4. **A backend unit test mirrored a line the primary frontend moved**:
   `test_review_display_mirrors_live_review_js` looked for `f.confidence<0.7` in
   `live-review.js`; the rule lives in `web/review-organization.js` as `.7` now. The test reads
   both files and both spellings.
5. **The developer page had no way to the client-errors page**: nav link and the "Recent
   errors" section now point at `client-errors.html` (PR #123's page); both surfaces kept.

### 72.4 Backend round trips added (`tests/api/test_report_signing.py`, 13 tests in all)

* A retried or double-submitted signing: the same `Idempotency-Key` while the first request
  holds the study's row lock is 409 `idempotency-key-in-flight` at once; after it completes the
  key replays the 201 with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and the same signature id; the same key
  with another body is 422; a fresh key is 409 `BASIS-REPORT-009`. One row, one PDF, one event.
* Firm isolation on every report route (404 for another firm's member on state, preview,
  files and sign; a viewer reads all three and gets 403 on sign).
* An archived study keeps and serves its signed report and state; an archived unsigned study
  cannot be previewed or signed (409 `BASIS-REPORT-007`) and its answers cannot change (409
  `BASIS-STUDY-004`).
* The new-revision path at the API level: the study at revision 2 with its export (the rows a
  reopen leaves), state is revision 2's (unsigned, `changed_since_signing` null), signing
  revision 1 is 409 `BASIS-REPORT-007`, `GET .../report` serves revision 2's draft by default and
  revision 1's signed PDF by number, revision 2 is signed on its own preview, both signed files
  then serve with their own sha256, the history lists both.

### 72.5 What this does not prove

* The live walkthrough used the lifecycle suite's offline providers and a synthetic index value
  (330.0 for 2025, labelled synthetic): the report's figures are not a study's, and the
  workflow's model steps were not exercised here (sections 6-50 did that).
* Sign-in token expiry (401 mid-session) and a request timeout were not simulated in the
  browser; the client's handlers (toast on 401, "Completion not verified" with retry on any
  failed state read) are covered by the node tests and the synthetic fixture
  (`web/tests/fixtures/report-completion.html`: unsigned, signed, changed, untracked, offline).
* The reopen's concurrency rule (two reopens, reopen while running) is #117's evidence
  (section 61); this section drove one reopen through the app.
* The Results page does not poll, so after the assets approval the engineer sees the export
  finish only on the next screen (FRONTEND_BACKLOG 9).

## 73. The developer page's workflow dialogs: what each step runs, on which systems, and what was measured (2026-11-02)

**Question.** The operator page (`web/developer/`, sections 67-71) had the step dialogs designed
but empty: every "Current runtime" cell read "Not reported", the runtime table listed two
names per step, and "Tests & results" was one sentence and four links. Can each dialog say what
the step's activity actually does, list every system the step uses with the exact model id,
provider, hosting and backup the worker runs, and show the architectures that were compared
with their measured numbers, without a figure typed by hand and without a word of study state?

**Standard.** OpenTelemetry's resource conventions name where a process runs from what the
process can read about itself (`cloud.platform`, e.g. `gcp_cloud_run`, detected from the
runtime environment: on Cloud Run the `K_SERVICE` variable), never from a service's name
(https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/resource/cloud/); the hosting labels follow that
rule and answer null otherwise. Status-page practice (Atlassian Statuspage, the GitHub and
Google Cloud status pages) reports a component's health apart from any customer's order or
incident; here, service health never says a study is signed or completed (section 71). For the
numbers, the documentation-as-code rule: a figure a page shows is copied from its source and a
test fails when the two diverge (the way `docs/api/openapi.json` is held to the app by
`test_openapi_contract.py`), so the content file is checked against EVAL_REPORT.md on every run.

**Setup.** Branch `claude/developer-workflow`, stacked on PR #125 (the developer page is not on
main yet: #125 carries the Codex working tree, and this change edits those files). No paid
call: the live stack is isolated (`pgvector/pgvector:pg16` container `devwf-pg` on 55435
migrated to 0028, the cost index store seeded from the bundled 2020 book, this checkout's API on
8500 with `OPS_OPERATOR_UIDS` set to one emulator account, a heartbeat script that builds the
real `WorkerRuntime` report from this checkout's settings with the provider probes answered by
an `httpx.MockTransport`, so the worker and relay rows are real `service_heartbeats` rows, the
web folder served on 3500 with a `local.html` that points `BASIS_CONFIG_OVERRIDES.apiBase` at
8500, the Auth emulator already on 9099). The `basis-web` compose stack, the other sessions'
containers and every client file were untouched.

### 73.1 What was built

* **`GET /v1/ops/health`, three additive fields per service** (OPS_HEALTH.md section 2,
  `basis/ops/services.py`, `basis/ops/hosting.py`, `basis/api/schemas/ops.py`, OpenAPI
  regenerated): `hosting`, a display label the runtime establishes (`Google Cloud Run` from
  `K_SERVICE`, `Docker container` from `/.dockerenv`, `Local process`; the worker's and relay's
  own label from their heartbeat reports; `Google Cloud SQL` / `Local PostgreSQL` /
  `Self-hosted PostgreSQL` and `Temporal Cloud` / `Local Temporal server` / `Self-hosted
  Temporal` from the API's settings; the providers by name; a self-hosted SAM 3 server by its
  `run.app` host; null when nothing establishes it, never a host name); `fallbacks`, the
  ordered backups as labels (`gpt-6.1-sol → OpenAI API · gpt-6.1-sol`), empty where the code
  has no fallback and null without a worker report; `models`, one structured route per worker
  setting that names a model (`VISION_MODEL` ... `CLASSIFY_MODEL`: model id, primary provider
  with its service id and the model or Azure deployment the request goes to, fallbacks in
  order). Nothing is inferred from a name: the labels come from the pool's routes in the
  worker's heartbeat (section 43's `model_routes()`).
* **`web/developer/workflow-content.json`**, the page's content: for each of the twelve steps
  three explanation steps written from the activity's code (each with the source file), the
  systems and model roles the runtime table lists, the measured results (up to three
  comparisons with the selected row first, up to eight metrics, the step's cost, tokens and
  latency where the report states them, the regression status from section 63) and the source
  links. Every figure is the report's own characters; 59 sections are cited with their GitHub
  anchors.
* **`backEnd/tests/unit/test_developer_workflow_content.py`** (50 tests) holds the file to the
  repository: each cited section is a heading of EVAL_REPORT.md and each figure (every table
  cell, metric, spend field and regression status) appears verbatim between that heading and
  the next of the same or a higher level; every link and explanation source is a path in the
  tree (a `#fragment` a heading of that Markdown file); every runtime row names a service id of
  the contract and a model role the worker reports; three steps per explanation, one value per
  column, no client data.
* **`web/developer/architecture.js`** renders the dialog from the content file and the health
  feed only: the runtime table shows the service row, then one row per model role with the
  provider's logo, the exact model id (and the Azure deployment when it differs), the
  provider's hosting and adapter and the model's backups, so SAM 3 plus a model is two rows
  with two logos; without a feed every system and role is listed as "Not reported" (a model id
  is never typed in the page); a role the worker does not run (the room call, surface crops,
  both off by default) is listed only when the feed reports it; the comparisons are tables
  with the selected architecture first, the metrics a table with a link to the section, the
  spend a line, the regression a line; a missing or malformed content file leaves the runtime
  table and says so. `health-model.js` keeps a `models` entry only when well formed.
  `web/tests/developer-workflow.test.cjs` (10 tests) covers the content shape, the inventory
  and photo dialogs with a synthetic feed (roles, logos, deployment, fallback, the off roles
  absent), the no-feed table, the verbatim figures and section links, a step with no paid
  call, the missing and malformed content file, escaping of hostile feed text, that no dialog
  says a study is signed or completed, and that every path resolves.

### 73.2 Verified in the browser

* Live, diagnostics connected (operator account): the systems list shows the hosting labels
  (`Local process`, `Local PostgreSQL`, `Local Temporal server`, `Study worker (Local
  process)`, `PostgreSQL (Local PostgreSQL)`, `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `Replicate`); the Build
  inventory dialog lists Room inventory (healthy), then `ROOM_MODEL` gpt-6-luna on OpenAI
  (OpenAI API, no backup) and `ROOM_MATERIALS_MODEL` claude-sonnet-5-5 on Anthropic, then
  Mask2Former (not enabled) and SAM 3 `vufinder/sam3@1bf97763d5df` on Replicate with the Meta
  logo; the room call and surface-crop roles are absent because this worker runs neither. The
  document itself (`ops_health.py` in the session scratchpad) lists every service with the
  three fields; `azure_openai` and `azure_di` are disabled (unset), with their hosting still
  named. All twelve dialogs open from the live page with the three sections and a selected
  row in each comparison that has one; counted from the DOM, the ten model-role rows across
  the dialogs (extract 2, photos 3, photo-results 1, inventory 2, assets 1) have no "Not
  reported" cell and one provider logo each. The cells that do read "Not reported" are the
  Model cells of services that report no model (the API, the database, Temporal, storage,
  sign-in, the relay), the page's existing convention.
* Not connected (`index.html`, the API unreachable): the Analyze photos dialog lists Photo
  analysis, the three roles and SAM 3, every cell "Not reported", and the measured results
  unchanged.
* Keyboard: the dialog opens from the step's button, Escape closes it and focus returns to
  that button (`data-step="inventory"`). Console on a fresh load of the live page: no message.
* 390 CSS px: `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` 390 for a 390 viewport and the dialog
  354 for 354; the runtime, comparison and metrics tables scroll inside the dialog, the
  explanation steps stack with arrows, the controls stay 44 px.

### 73.3 Decisions a reviewer may ask about

* *Why a checked-in JSON and not a generator?* The explanations are written from the code, not
  derivable from the report; the figures are the report's. A generator would have to decide
  which 59 of 9,300 lines matter. The test is the generator's guarantee without the generator:
  change a number in the report and the test names the cell.
* *Why `hosting` is null so often.* The API knows its own process, its database URL and its
  Temporal address; the worker knows its own process and the localizer URL. Nothing else is
  known, so nothing else is said (the hand-off asked that `Temporal` alone never mean Temporal
  Cloud).
* *Why `fallbacks` distinguishes `[]` from null.* "None configured" and "not known" are
  different facts for an operator; the page already drew them differently.
* *Links go to `blob/main`.* Sections 64-72 exist only on the open PR branches until they merge;
  the test resolves every link and anchor against the checkout, which is the stricter check.
* *Tokens per step.* The report gives per-study totals (section 40: 2.8 M input, 165 K output
  for the 724-call study) and per-call figures in places (33.12, 32.9); the dialogs show what
  the report has and "Not measured" otherwise, never a split invented from the totals.

### 73.4 Not done

* An authenticated run-record API (list, detail, download of `backEnd/evals/` manifests and
  ledgers, as `claude-handoff.md` describes) is not built; the dialogs link to the record
  format and the registry module. The figures on the page are the report's, not read from
  run directories.
* The "Recent errors" section stays the link to `client-errors.html` (PR #123).
* The page's own expiry display of `expires_at` and `last_inference` rendering (ops-health
  hand-over) are unchanged.

**Measured.** Web: 331 node tests pass (321 before). Backend: `tests/unit/ops` 90 passed (65
before; `test_hosting.py` 20 new, `test_services.py` 5 new), `test_developer_workflow_content.py`
50 passed; `tests/api/test_ops_health.py` extended with the three fields on the real-heartbeat
document; the full backend suite 6,612 passed, 23 skipped, 76 subtests (21 min 32 s; unit, integration and slow, provider keys unset). Static gates green (`ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, the
catalogue, the OpenAPI document, the rule fingerprints, the client-data guard).

## 74. Evaluation run records for operators: `GET /v1/ops/eval-runs` and the dialogs' "Run records" (2026-11-02)

**Question.** Section 73 left one piece of the developer page's hand-off open: the figures in
the step dialogs are the report's, copied and checked, but the evidence behind them, the run
directories the registry reads (section 43), could be seen only with `python -m evals.registry`
on the machine that holds the data. Can a platform operator read those records through the API,
with every field the registry has (component and version, prompts, models, labels and split,
results, measured metrics, tokens, cost, duration, the tested commit), download the manifest,
the report, the ledger and the console log, and see them under each step's results, without a
path, a host name or a key leaving the host, without a run ever being compared to a run scored
on other labels, and without a host that has no data ever looking like a host with no runs?

**Standard.** The experiment trackers expose a run's record through an authenticated read API
with the same fields the UI shows and the artifacts as downloads behind the same check: MLflow's
REST API (`runs/search` with filters and a page token, `runs/get`, artifacts listed and
downloaded through the tracking server, never as static files), Weights & Biases' run files
API. Keyset pagination with an opaque cursor is what this API already does for the timeline,
the activity and the browser errors (sections 41, 55, 65). For the figures, the rule of
section 43 stands: a backfilled manifest says `unknown` where the files did not say, and the
API must keep that as null rather than a number; and a figure the registry derives (a cost
summed from the price table, a duration estimated from file times) has to say so, so the page
can tell a measurement from an estimate.

**Setup.** Branch `claude/eval-run-records-api`, stacked on `claude/developer-workflow` (section
73, PR #126). No paid call anywhere. The browser check ran on an isolated stack: this checkout's
API in `dev` on 8600 with no database (`TEMPORAL_ADDRESS` pointed at a closed port, so the
health feed is the 503 document), `OPS_OPERATOR_UIDS` set to one account created in the Auth
emulator already on 9099, `BASIS_EVAL_DATA_DIR` a synthetic directory built by the API test's
own fixtures (one run recorded by the real `evals.record.EvalRun` with a scripted model, a
backfilled manifest, a stopped run, an appraisal run with non-finite scores, a run inside the
verification tree, a manifest that is not JSON and one that is not a run manifest); a second API
on 8601 without the variable; the web folder served on 3600 from a symlinked copy with a
`developer/local.html` whose `BASIS_CONFIG_OVERRIDES.apiBase` is 8600. The other sessions'
ports and the compose stack were untouched. The real registry was read once, read only
(`python -m evals.registry --json`), to see the shapes the API has to carry: 356 runs, 351
backfilled, label entries carrying the absolute path of the label file.

### 74.1 What was built

* **Three routes** (`basis/api/routes/eval_runs.py`, `basis/api/schemas/eval_runs.py`,
  docs/api/EVAL_RUNS.md, OpenAPI regenerated): `GET /v1/ops/eval-runs` (filters `component`,
  repeated as OR because a step lists several, `model` with the registry's `M*` prefix,
  `labels`, `dataset`, `split`, `status`, `release`; `limit` 1 to 200; a keyset `cursor`;
  `total`), `GET /v1/ops/eval-runs/{run_id}` (the item plus settings, environment without the
  host name, harness options, a backfilled manifest's provenance, notes, error) and
  `GET /v1/ops/eval-runs/{run_id}/files/{manifest|report|ledger|console}` (attachments through
  the operator check). The same `require_operator` as the health and browser-error routes, 60
  reads a minute per operator, no database at all. `run_id` is the directory's relative path
  as base64url: opaque on the wire, reversible, validated, and looked up only in the cached
  scan, so the API never opens a path a client named.
* **The read layer** (`basis/ops/eval_runs.py`) over `evals.registry` (`run_directories`,
  `tree_directories`, `read_run`: nothing re-implemented): a catalogue scanned at most once
  per 30 s per process, off the event loop, one scan at a time; a directory the registry
  cannot read becomes a record with `record.error` instead of failing the list; the projection
  turns every `unknown` into null, keeps the cost's source (`ledger`: summed from the recorded
  calls; `summary`: the runner's `run.json` figure, what the backfill copied) and the
  duration's (`recorded`: the runner's clock; `file_times`: the backfill's estimate, which on
  the real data runs to 13 days for a 52-photo run), takes token totals only from recorded
  calls, and drops the label paths. `RunEntry` in the registry gained the fields the API needs
  (split and repeats from the manifest or the latest scoring, wall seconds, token totals, exit
  code, settings, environment, options, provenance, notes, format), so the CLI's JSON carries
  them too.
* **Availability is a fact, not an empty list.** `BASIS_EVAL_DATA_DIR` is now a setting
  (`eval_data_dir`, config.py and `.env.example`). Unset (every deployed host), a directory that
  does not exist, or the evaluation tooling not installed (the production image ships
  `basis/` alone, so the `evals` import is optional and the module says so): every route answers
  404 `eval-data-unavailable`, `BASIS-API-046`, with the reason in `detail`. `BASIS-API-047` is
  a file over the 8 MiB bound.
* **Redaction before anything leaves.** The detail and the files mask credential-named
  fields (the logging rule), API-key-shaped strings and credential headers, the host name, and
  replace the data directory by `<data dir>` and any `/Users/<name>` or `/home/<name>` by `~`
  in every path (the manifest's command line, the options, the backfilled label paths, the
  console log). The payload files (prompts, model answers) are never served.
* **A run's standing against the pipeline, computed, not typed.** `pipeline_prompts(settings)`
  lists every prompt the configured pipeline runs with its version and the model the setting
  names, read the way the activities read them (the photo mode, count fusion, the room step
  and its second look, the room call, surface crops, the grounded reading, the fallback, the
  classifier); `tests/unit/ops/test_eval_runs.py` holds it to `worker.main.pipeline_models` on
  four settings variants, so the two readings of the pipeline cannot drift. `selection.status`
  is `current` when every prompt the run names is that version on a model a pipeline setting
  names for it, `alternative` when a version, a model or a prompt differs, `not_in_pipeline`
  when none of its prompts is run, `unknown` when the run names no prompt; `reasons` says which.
  It is relative to this API process's settings (the deployment's); the worker's effective
  routes stay on `GET /v1/ops/health`.
* **The page.** `web/developer/workflow-content.json` maps each step to its registry
  components (`components`; the four reviews and Upload and Report & sign have none;
  `test_developer_workflow_content.py` checks each is a released prompt name or a
  `HARNESS_COMPONENTS` value). `architecture.js` ends "Tests & results" with a "Run records"
  block: one table per label set and split, never one across them; the standing badge; the
  headline metric per dataset; cost and duration each with their source; tokens; the code with
  the dirty flag; results as `passed / failed / test errors`; the record's kind (recorded,
  backfilled, `run.json` only, unreadable with the error); "Not recorded" for every null; the
  four file buttons, which fetch through the authenticated client (an `<a href>` cannot carry
  the token) and save the attachment under the API's name (`Content-Disposition` is now
  exposed by CORS, with a client-side fallback); "Load older runs" for the next page. Every
  feed state has its own sentence: not connected, loading, untrusted origin, sign-in failure,
  timeout, network, 401, 403, 404 with the no-data reason, 404 otherwise, 429, another status, a
  malformed body, and "the registry has no run that names these components; runs of other
  components exist on this host". `health-client.js` gained `evalRuns` and `evalRunFile`;
  `health-page.js` reads once per dialog opening while connected.

### 74.2 Verified

* **API, no database** (`tests/api/test_eval_runs.py`, 23 tests): 401 without a token; a firm
  owner, and anyone on an empty allowlist, 403 `not-operator` without diagnostics; unset,
  missing and tooling-absent hosts 404 `BASIS-API-046` with the reason; the list newest first
  with every field as the fixtures recorded them (the real run: the prompt's released version
  and sha256, the tested commit of this checkout with its dirty flag, 1,000 input and 20 output
  tokens, cost from the ledger, duration recorded; the backfilled run: commit, dirty flag and
  sha256 null, cost from the summary, duration from file times, the label's path gone); the
  broken manifests listed with their errors; NaN scores null; the tree link not a second run;
  no local path, home directory, host name or key in any list, detail or file; every filter;
  pages walking every run once, 422 for the bounds and a bad cursor; eight ids the host did not
  issue 404; the four files with their media types and names, the manifest's host name `***`
  and command line paths replaced, the ledger's `api_key` masked and its error text redacted,
  the console log redacted, the backfilled run's report its `eval.md`; 413 over the bound; the
  scan cached and refreshed after the TTL; 60 reads a minute then 429.
* **Browser** (desktop and 390 CSS px): with diagnostics connected, Analyze photos shows two
  tables, `photo_components_v1 · split dev` (the recorded run, Alternative: gpt-4o-mini is not
  the pipeline's VISION_MODEL) and `photo_components_v1 · split not recorded` (the backfilled
  run, cost "$1.10 runner's summary", duration "13.0 days estimated from file times", code "Not
  recorded"); Build inventory shows the in-tree run as "Current pipeline"; Review appraisal says
  no run record applies; Produce results says the registry has no run that names
  `study_export`. The Ledger button saved `countables_v3_mini.llm_calls.jsonl` (the Manifest
  button `countables_v3_mini.manifest.json` once the header was exposed; before that the
  fallback name). Reloaded and not connected, the block asks to connect and names the
  components. Against the API without the variable, the block shows the API's sentence
  ("BASIS_EVAL_DATA_DIR is not set ..."). Keyboard: Return on a focused step opens its dialog
  with focus on Close, Escape closes it and focus returns to that step. 390 px: page scroll
  width 390, dialog 354 wide, the run tables scroll inside their regions (320 of 1,380), the
  file buttons 44 px. Console: only the health feed's 503 resource messages (this stack has no
  database), none from the page's scripts.
* **Real data, read only**: the registry over `~/basis-eval-data` reads 356 runs in under two
  seconds; the API's redaction was written against what those manifests carry (absolute label
  paths, `unknown` strings, `hostname` in the environment).

### 74.3 Decisions a reviewer may ask about

* *Why 404 and not 200 with an empty list for a host without data.* The brief asked that an
  empty host never look like "no runs". A problem with its own type and code is the only
  answer a client cannot mistake; the page shows the reason.
* *Why the API process's settings decide "current".* The worker's routes are in its heartbeat,
  which needs the database; these routes need none and run on the machine with the data. The
  deployment's settings are the same file; the doc says which it is, and the page labels the
  badge "Current pipeline" with the reasons as a tooltip.
* *Why group by label file and split only.* Within one label set, the architectures and models
  are the comparison the registry exists for; the dataset is what makes two runs comparable.
  Repeats are shown per run, not used to split tables.
* *Why serve the manifest with paths replaced rather than verbatim.* The hand-off forbids
  local file paths through the page; `<data dir>` and `~` keep the file readable and the
  record's shape intact. The payload files are not served at all: they are the prompts.
* *Why the registry's `RunEntry` grew instead of the API re-reading manifests.* One reader. The
  CLI's JSON now carries the same fields, and `test_registry.py` holds them.

### 74.4 Not done

* No filter on the page: the block lists the step's components and lets the API's order stand;
  the registry CLI keeps `--matrix` and the other filters.
* The developer page's other open items (section 73.4) are unchanged.

**Measured.** See the test ledger (`backEnd/tests/LEDGER.md`, "Evaluation run records for
operators"): `tests/unit/ops/test_eval_runs.py` 19, `tests/api/test_eval_runs.py` 23,
`test_registry.py` 12, `test_developer_workflow_content.py` 62; web 340 node tests pass (331
before). Static gates green (`ruff`, `ruff format`, `mypy`, the catalogue, the OpenAPI
document, the rule fingerprints, the client-data guard). Unit suite 5,003 passed, 10 skipped (1 min 49 s); integration and slow suite 1,668 passed, 7 skipped, 79 subtests, one failure (`tests/integration/db/test_retention_purge.py::test_an_object_already_gone_is_reported_not_fatal`, the retention purge from section 54, untouched here; it passed alone right after, so it is an ordering or timing flake of that suite, left for its owner), 19 min 34 s, provider keys unset.

## 75. Temporal's deadlock detector and image work on the worker's event loop (2026-11-02)

**Question.** Main's CI failed three lifecycle tests on 2026-11-02 within 90 s
(`test_conventions.py::test_an_assets_correction_classifies_the_firms_next_study`,
`test_localization.py::test_rooms_reject_relocalizes_only_the_reanalyzed_photo[components_gate]`,
`test_reject_paths.py::test_two_rejections_in_a_row_keep_counting_revisions`), each a status
query refused with `TMPRL1101` "Potential deadlock detected: workflow didn't yield within 2
second(s)", 2.3 to 4.2 s after the test's worker started. They passed on rerun and in every run
since. What makes the SDK report a deadlock, can it happen to a real study, and what is fixed?

**Setup.** temporalio 1.34.0 (Python), the lifecycle harness (time-skipping server, real
Postgres, real worker), Python 3.12 on an Apple M-series laptop. No paid call; the photos are
synthetic.

**Method.**

1. Read the SDK: `_WorkflowWorker._handle_activation` runs the activation on a thread and waits
   for it with `asyncio.wait_for(task, 2)` on the worker's event loop
   (`temporalio/worker/_workflow.py`, `_deadlock_timeout_seconds`, fixed at 2 s unless
   `debug_mode`). The timer is a loop timer: if the loop is held for 2 s, it fires before the
   activation's finished result is processed, so a quick activation reads as a deadlock. The
   async activities run on that same loop.
2. Timed a full sandboxed replay of every recorded history (`tests/lifecycle/histories/`,
   `Replayer`, three runs each).
3. Ran the three tests, then the whole lifecycle suite, with asyncio debug mode (slow callbacks
   over 0.1 s) and a watchdog thread that samples the loop thread's stack whenever the loop has
   not ticked for 0.3 s (then 0.08 s).
4. Listed the CPU work that `async def` code calls directly, and timed the heaviest
   (`prepare_image`: decode, orient, downsize to 1,024 px, re-encode) on a synthetic 4000 x 3000
   JPEG (4.2 MB), alone and with 20 activities started together, the way a study's photo
   activities start; the worst loop stall was measured by a 5 ms ticker.

| measurement | result |
|---|---|
| full replay, longest history (`components_gate`, 288 events) | 0.020 s |
| full replay, cold first run (`appraisal_reject`, 175 events) | 0.079 s |
| lifecycle suite under the watchdog: stalls over 0.3 s | only at session start: the Postgres container (0.9 s) and the SDK's default build id, computed once per process from every loaded module (0.7 s, memoized) |
| `prepare_image`, one 12 MP photo | 0.083 s (median of 5) |
| 20 photos at once, on the loop | worst stall 1.70 to 1.82 s; wall 1.70 to 1.82 s (3 runs) |
| 20 photos at once, `prepare_image_in_thread` | worst stall 0.020 to 0.068 s; wall 0.28 to 0.33 s (3 runs) |

**Findings.**

* Replay is about 100 times under the limit, so the workflow code is not what took 2 s. The
  reported deadlocks were the loop being held, not the workflow.
* The CI trigger was not reproduced: locally nothing in the lifecycle suite holds the loop
  near 2 s after start-up, the fixtures are 800 x 600 photos, and the three failures landed
  within 90 s of each other on one runner. A stall of the runner is the likeliest cause; it
  is not proven.
* Production has the mechanism at full size. `prepare_image` ran directly in `async def` in
  `analyze_photo` (both vision paths), `localize_photo` and the room step, and the segmenter,
  the surface crops (decode, the full-size blend, the crop JPEG, the request's two prepared
  images), SAM 3 tiling and the UAD upload parse did CPU work on the loop too. Twenty photos
  held the loop 1.7 s on this laptop, so a host at half its speed, or a study with more
  photos, crosses 2 s: workflow tasks fail as deadlocks (the server retries them after the
  task timeout) and the API's status queries fail.
* A naive fix would have added a bug: `prepare_image` used `warnings.catch_warnings`, which
  swaps the process-wide filter list and is not thread-safe. On main's code, eight threads
  preparing at once left a process-wide `error` filter for Pillow's warning behind in 3 runs
  of 3.

**Change.**

* `basis.vision.prep.prepare_image_in_thread` (`asyncio.to_thread`) at every async call site;
  the segmenter's encode, the crops' decode and blend and request, tiling and the upload parse
  on threads as well. Pillow releases the GIL while it decodes and resamples, so the batch is
  also faster (1.7 s to 0.3 s for 20 photos).
* `prepare_image` no longer touches the warning filters. `MAX_PIXELS` (80 M) is below Pillow's
  warning threshold (89.5 M), so every image Pillow would warn about is refused from its header
  as `too_many_pixels` (it was `not_an_image`), before a pixel is decoded; Pillow's
  `DecompressionBombError` (twice its threshold) is still `not_an_image`.
* `tests/unit/test_event_loop_image_work.py` walks `basis/` and refuses a direct call to the
  known image functions inside `async def` (it found the six call sites on main); the
  `tests/unit/vision/test_prep.py` additions are listed in the test ledger. `AGENTS.md`
  states the rule.

**Verdict.** Fixed for the cause found in production code; the CI failures' own trigger is
unproven. No workflow code changed, so no patch is needed and the recorded histories replay
as before.

**Open.**

* If `TMPRL1101` recurs in CI, run the failing test file with the watchdog described in
  method 3 to name what holds the loop.
* The worker has no loop-stall metric. A production worker could export the worst stall per
  minute the same way, and an alert on it would show a blocking call before studies slow
  down.
* The guard knows the functions measured here by name; CPU work under another name is caught
  only by review.

**Measured.** Unit suite 5,012 passed, 10 skipped; lifecycle suite 118 passed, 5 skipped;
image and upload slow tests 142 passed; static gates green.

## 76. A study cancelled from the app can be restarted: `POST .../cancel` is a Temporal cancellation (2026-11-02)

**Question.** Section 62.5 recorded, and left open, that a study cancelled through
`POST .../cancel` could not be restarted. Is that still so on main, why, and what is the
standard fix?

**Setup.** The real API and outbox against the Temporal dev server with the test workflow
(`tests/integration/api/test_start_to_decision.py`), and the real workflow on the
time-skipping server (`tests/lifecycle/`). No paid call.

**Method and findings.**

1. Reproduced on main through the routes: start, cancel, restart. The execution closed with
   status `COMPLETED`, and restart answered 409 `study-completed`.
2. Cause: the route sent the workflow's `cancel_study` signal. The workflow stopped its work and
   returned normally, so Temporal recorded the execution `COMPLETED` (outcome `cancelled` only
   inside its result). Restart accepts an execution that closed without completing and starts
   under `ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY`, which also refuses a completed one. The API test passed
   because its in-memory service reported `CANCELED`, a status the real path never produced.
3. The standard: Temporal's way to stop a workflow is a cancellation request
   (`WorkflowHandle.cancel`). The workflow receives `CancelledError`, cleans up and re-raises,
   and the execution closes `CANCELED`. `StudyWorkflow` already handled that path (section 3 of
   S2_SPEC; `test_temporal_cancellation_records_the_outcome`).
4. Measured on both servers: Temporal accepts a cancellation request for an execution that has
   already closed, completed or cancelled, and ignores it. The status is unchanged and no error
   is returned. The signal's "not found" answer for a closed execution therefore has no
   equivalent, so the service describes the execution first. A second request while the first is
   being handled is accepted.

**Change.**

* `TemporalWorkflowService.cancel` describes the execution (409 `workflow-closed` unless it is
  running) and then sends `handle.cancel(reason=...)`. The reason is on the history's
  cancel-request event and, as before, on the study's timeline (`study.cancel_requested`).
* `StudyWorkflow`, on `CancelledError`, sets its cancel reason before it stops the work, as the
  signal does, so the decide and retry validators refuse while it stops. This is in-memory state
  only, with no command change, so the recorded histories replay (the lifecycle suite's
  versioning tests). The signal handler stays, because recorded histories carry it.
* `POST .../start` on a cancelled study now answers 409 `workflow-closed`, which is
  `ensure_not_ended_unsuccessfully`'s stated intent; before, it answered 202 with the closed run.
  `POST .../restart` is the way back.
* Studies cancelled before this change stay `COMPLETED` and cannot be restarted; archive and
  re-create them (docs/api/GATE_DRAFTS_AND_RESUME.md). Nothing is deployed, so only local
  development data is affected.

| check | main | after |
|---|---|---|
| execution status after `POST .../cancel` | `COMPLETED` | `CANCELED` |
| `POST .../restart` after it | 409 `study-completed` | 202, revision 2, new run |
| real workflow: cancel, restart, approve every gate | not possible | completed on revision 2; runs `cancelled`, `completed` |
| cancel of a closed execution | 409 `workflow-closed` | 409 `workflow-closed` (by describe) |

**Verdict.** Fixed with Temporal's standard cancellation. The regression tests fail on main's
service and pass after the change.

**Open.** Nothing from this section. Section 62.5's other item, archive racing a restart, is
unchanged.

**Measured.** Lifecycle suite: 122 passed, 5 skipped, including the four new cancel tests and the
archive test's route-level restart. Unit suite: 5,004 passed. Integration API tests: 4 passed.
Static gates are green.

## 77. The cost index is fetched by default, and a study asks for its own cost year (2026-11-02)

**Question.** Bryan's decision (2026-11-02) is to switch the public cost index on, and when a
study's year is not loaded, to go and get it. How does a study choose its year today, what
happens when the year is missing, and what changes?

**How a study chooses its year and place (unchanged).** Cost segregation prices each asset at
its cost when the property was placed in service. The cost year is the year of the intake's
`placed_in_service_date`; without an intake it is the appraisal's effective-date year, and with
neither it is `COST_YEAR`. The location factor is the RSMeans row for the intake's ZIP or state,
else the appraisal's subject state. The year factor is the Historical Cost Index of that year over
the 2020 book's Jan. 1, 2020 base of 239.1 (COST_INDICES.md, sections 45 and 47).

**What happened before.** A study priced with whatever the index store held when its assets step
ran. Only the refresh job fetched, which is documented for a monthly scheduler that nothing
configures, and fetching was off by default. A study placed in service after 2020 was therefore
priced at the 2020 book's index, with every cost row flagged `cost:YEAR_INDEX_MISSING`. That was
30 % under the purchase price on the live CA 2024 studies (section 45). With the 2024 value
loaded the gap closed to about 2 % (sections 47 and 49).

**Change.**

* `COST_INDEX_FETCH` defaults to `on` in dev, staging and prod, and to `off` in test
  (`Settings.cost_index_fetching`, the precedent of `RATE_LIMIT_STORE`), so no test reaches the
  network. Setting it explicitly wins everywhere.
* `process_assets` (`_ensure_cost_year`) chooses the year exactly as pricing does
  (`TakeoffPlan.build` over the store's values). When that year has no published index, it runs
  the refresh job once before classifying, with no database connection held and bounded by
  `COST_INDEX_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S`. The run is recorded with `trigger = study`, and `_write` reads the
  store again, so the study prices with the fetched value. A source that cannot answer leaves the
  year flagged as before, and the fetch never fails the study. A year in the released book (1970
  to 2020) or already loaded asks nothing.
* The live source was checked today, read-only and without the database:

| year | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RSMeans Historical Cost Index, July (Gordian's public pages) | 257.5 | 297.1 | 293.7 | 294.8 | 300.7 | 314.5 |

All six were read with no failures and none provisional. They match the values recorded in
section 47.

**Licensing.** Bryan's decision for now (2026-11-02): one unit-cost table serves every firm.
That table is the one Basis has today, transcribed from the RSMeans 2020 Residential and Building
books (`COST_TABLE_PATH`, private, never in the repository). The cost index trends it to each
study's cost year. Firms do not upload tables. Instead, the firm's contract confirms that every
employee who uses Basis holds their own RSMeans license, and a firm that signs without one bears
that. This may change as Basis grows. Only the public index is fetched here; the unit-cost table
is never fetched or bundled.

**Open.**

* A study priced while its year's July value was still provisional keeps that value until it is
  repriced (`POST .../assets/reprice`). The refresh job replaces provisional values only when it
  runs, and nothing schedules it yet. The study-time fetch fills missing years, not provisional
  ones.
* Location factors after 2020 are not published on the public pages. The 2020 book's location
  table applies, as before.

**Measured.** `tests/integration/db/test_cost_year_on_demand.py`: 5 passed.
`tests/unit/costs/test_refresh_cli.py`: 5 passed. The live fetch is shown above.

## 78. Fail safe: no substitute value reaches a report's dollars (2026-11-02)

**Question.** Bryan's rule (2026-11-02): when an input the money needs is missing or unreadable,
or a model call fails, Basis must stop and say what is missing, never fill the gap with a
placeholder, a typical value, a setting or mock data that then prices the study. Where did the
pipeline substitute, and what changes?

**Method.**

1. Three read-only audits, one for each of these areas: appraisal and intake; quantities, costs
   and the building model; vision, classification, the gates, the report and signing.
2. Every high-impact claim was checked against the code, and three of them by running the code
   (the basement area, the stories truncation, the classifier's default class).

**Found on main.** Nothing stopped on a flag. Approving a gate, exporting and signing checked no
review reason. Only a withheld allocation (unreconciled, or no building cost new) kept a report
from being rendered. These values reached dollars:

| what was substituted | where | flagged? |
|---|---|---|
| six legacy "typical RSMeans" placeholder rows (light fixtures, outlets, carpet, tile, cabinets, HVAC units), looked up **before** the real cost table | `domain/costs.py` | no |
| typical room area (or 150 SF) when there was no GLA, garage area, or basement area, for exterior rooms, and for components in no room | `measurements.room_areas`, `_room_takeoff` | no |
| a lone basement room with no basement area sized GLA × 150 SF (277,500 SF for a 1,850 SF house) | `measurements.room_areas` | no |
| 1.5 stories truncated to 1 (the field was an `int`; the measurement dropped non-whole counts), then 1 story assumed for the footprint, smoke alarms and model type | extraction, `measurements`, `structure` | model only |
| a basement finish taken as 100 % when not printed | `measurements`, `structure` | no |
| a count of 1 when the component had none | `process_assets._count` | no |
| the room's perimeter used as the cabinet run (and the countertop on it) | `takeoffs` | no |
| the total depreciation used as physical depreciation | `structure.depreciation` | no |
| `COST_LOCATION_FACTOR` (1.0) when no ZIP or state resolved | `measurements.resolve_cost_index` | no |
| unpriced rows' share spread over the priced rows | `evidence/result` | listed |
| a default building class (27.5 / 39 years) when the classifier failed | `classify/router._fallback` | flagged, not blocking |
| the uniform factor scaling the schedule to the basis when there were no appraisal fields | `evidence/result` | flagged, not blocking |
| any pricing error (a cost year before the index, a table on another base year) reported as "no cost row" | `process_assets._cost` | mislabelled |

**Change.**

* **Placeholder prices removed.** Light fixtures, outlets and HVAC units now price from rows
  already transcribed from Bryan's RSMeans 2020 books. Carpet (09 68 16.10 0701 + pad
  09 68 10.10 9401, p. 510) and floor tile (09 31 33.10 3270, p. 500) were read from the page
  images and added to the private table, with backups kept. The table builder now keeps rows
  it does not produce: a rebuild had dropped four.
* **Rows held by a missing input are unpriced.** A row whose quantity would stand on a
  substitute is written with quantity 0, no cost, the review reason `input:<code>` and its cost
  row reading `missing input: <what>`. This covers no GLA, stories, garage area, basement area
  or finish, an exterior room, no room, a room of unknown type, no count, and a guessed cabinet
  run. A counted item does not use the room's area and still prices.
* **The two bugs are fixed.** Half stories are kept (the field is a decimal, so the 1-1/2 and
  2-1/2 story models are used). Basement rooms are sized only on a printed basement area.
* **Depreciation and the building model.** Depreciation is physical, else the age-life ratio of
  the printed ages, else none. The building model records its assumed inputs (class, type,
  basement finish, cost-data date). Pricing errors are named.
* **The report is withheld while a blocker remains.** The result lists every `blocker` with what
  is missing, how many assets it holds and where it is fixed. While one remains the allocation
  is withheld, so no report is rendered and none can be signed, and the skip reason names each
  (docs/api/STUDY_RESULT.md). The blockers are the row inputs, `unpriced`, `unclassified`,
  `appraisal_fields`, `building_rcn`, `depreciation`, `cost_index` and the study inputs
  (`input:location`, `input:cost_year`, `input:model_class`, `input:cost_data_date`). The
  uniform-factor allocation can no longer produce a report.
* **The engineer can supply a measurement.** An `asset` correction at the assets review may
  carry `quantity`, `quantity_unit` and `quantity_source`. These are checked by the decisions
  route (422) and by the activity (`BASIS-CORRECT-043`). The measurement replaces the computed
  quantity and clears the missing input.
* **Every blocker is recorded for the operators (Bryan, 2026-11-02).** One `client_errors` record
  (kind `study_input`, `BASIS-STUDY-037`, migration 0029) is written per blocker per revision.
  It carries the firm, the person whose decision started the run, the study, the blocker, the
  assets it holds and every file the study has. Records group into one issue per firm and
  blocker on the operator page (docs/api/CLIENT_ERRORS.md 4.1).

**What is not a substitute, and stays (priced, with the assumption on the row).** These are
published methods applied to inputs the study has: RSMeans' square-foot model, the GLA shared
over the rooms by typical weights, 240 SF per garage car, a wall area at an 8-foot ceiling, the
NEC minimum outlets per room, and roof pitch and wall height constants. They also include
inputs no appraisal carries and every study estimates, such as a buried utility lateral and
the two exterior doors of the small systems (flagged `structure:assumed_quantity`).

**Verdict.** No value substituted for a missing input reaches a report's dollars. A study
missing one stops before the report, says what is missing and where to fix it, and is recorded
for the operators. Studies that were priced on substitutes before are now withheld until the
engineer supplies the input; that is the intended change.

**Open.**

* A firm-specific unit cost (a row the shared table lacks) is added to the table by an operator.
  There is no per-study cost entry, matching the shared-table decision.
* Opening a firm's files from the operator page: built in section 79 (support opens them with a
  reason; the firm sees every open).
* Vision fallbacks that keep a real model output (the count fusion falling back to the base
  call, the room step's heuristic merge, a failed material second look) are flagged on the
  photo or room, not blocking; propagating them to the assets is the next step.
* The web app shows neither `blockers` nor the measured-quantity fields yet (FRONTEND_BACKLOG 10).

## 79. Basis support can open a firm's files, and the firm sees every open (2026-11-02)

**Question.** A missing-input record (section 78) lists the files a study has, but nobody at
Basis could look at them: a firm's studies are visible only to its members. Bryan decided
(2026-11-02) that support may open them, without the firm approving each time: the product is
new, it is not yet known that every step works, and the first firms are not comfortable with
technology, so support has to see what they uploaded to help. How should that access work so a
firm can trust it?

**The standard.** A cloud provider's access-transparency log (Google Cloud Access
Transparency) records each access by its staff to a customer's content: the resource, the time,
the justification (for example customer-initiated support, with the case) and the person, and
the customer reads the log. A stricter step, Access Approval (Microsoft calls it Customer
Lockbox), makes the customer approve each access first. Bryan chose the first without the
second while the product is new.

**What was built** (docs/api/OPS_DOCUMENTS.md):

* `GET /v1/ops/studies/{id}/documents` lists a study's files with the uploader and the firm;
  `.../documents/{id}/content?reason=` returns one file's bytes. Platform operators only
  (`OPS_OPERATOR_UIDS`); a firm role, owner included, gets 403 and nothing is recorded.
* A reason is required (3 to 300 characters). `client_error_id` names the record the open came
  from.
* **Every open is recorded before the bytes are read**: an append-only `study_events` row,
  `operator.document_accessed`, with actor `operator` (migration 0030 adds the actor), the
  operator's user, the document, the reason, the record, and the file's name, kind, sha256 and
  size. The firm reads it on its study's timeline. The downgrade refuses while such a row
  exists rather than delete an access record. An open whose bytes are gone (the retention purge)
  stays recorded, because the access was granted. A refused open records nothing.
* **Never cached**: `no-store`, no `ETag`, no 304. Each open is answered, so each is recorded,
  and the operator's browser keeps no copy.
* **The developer page**: a missing-input record lists its files with an Open button. The page
  asks for the reason (prefilled with the record's kind, blocker and id) and shows the file in
  the page with a Download link. Only images and PDFs are shown inline. An XML, a ZIP or text is
  a download only, because markup in it would run with the page's origin from a `blob:` URL.

**Verified.**

* `tests/api/test_ops_documents.py` covers:
  - listing and opening as an operator who is not a member of the firm;
  - the headers;
  - one row per open, with no cache answer;
  - the firm's own timeline showing the open;
  - every refusal (no reason, short or long reason, malformed record id, not an operator, the
    owner, another firm, unknown study or document, an unconfirmed upload), with nothing
    recorded;
  - bytes gone: 404, with the access still recorded.
* The migration test covers the operator actor, the refused unknown actor, the clean downgrade
  with no rows, and the refused downgrade with one.
* Live check on an isolated local stack (Postgres in its own container, the API on 8200 from
  this branch, the web on 3400, the local Auth emulator, test accounts only):
  - The operator signed in and opened the photo and the synthetic PDF from a `study_input`
    record. The firm owner's `GET .../timeline` showed the three opens with each reason and the
    record id.
  - The check found one bug, fixed before the PR: the first version opened a new tab after the
    request, and the browser blocked it (`window.open` returned no window). The page now shows
    the file in place.
  - It also found the file table's names running into their types, a style fix.

**Not modelled, and open.**

* The firm does not approve each access (Access Approval). Revisit once the product is stable.
* The firm's app shows the timeline row with the actor word "Operator". It should read "Basis
  support opened <file>: <reason>" (FRONTEND_BACKLOG 11).
* The firm's contract should say Basis support may view its uploads for support. That is
  Bryan's to write, not a code change.
* Listing the files records nothing on the timeline (names and sizes, no content). The API log
  has a line for it.

## 80. The comparison tables, written for people (2026-11-02)

Bryan, reading 15.1 and the developer page's step dialogs: the tables named setups the way
their harnesses did ("4c. sol low + Opus medium per class, leave-one-photo-out"), named models
by nickname without the exact id, effort or temperature, gave no tokens, and some steps had no
comparison for some of their parts. Nothing was re-run for this section: every figure is the
one already printed; what was added was read from the run records and the code.

What changed, in the 32 comparison tables the developer page shows or that its parts lead to
(15.1, 16.2, 17.1, 23.3, 25.2, 26.2, 26.3, 26.8, 28.1, 28.2, 28.3, 32.5, 32.6, 32.10, 33.4, 33.5,
33.12, 35.2 (two), 39, 39.4, 42.5, 44.3, 45.3, 47.3, 48.4, 49.3, 53, 54, 55, 63, 72.2):

- **How to read this table** above each: the question it answered, what each column measures
  and which way is better (↑ / ↓).
- Each row starts with its old id (4c, d2, run 5) and a plain name, then a **Models** column:
  every call's exact model id, provider, reasoning effort and temperature as sent, and a
  **Tokens** column. Tables printed with setups as columns (63, 53, 42.5, 72.2, 39.4, 35.2,
  45.3, 47.3, 33.4) are turned so each setup is a row; 33.5's grouped table (several models a
  row, figures separated by `/`) is split into one row per model.
- A key at the top of the report gives every short model name's exact id, provider and price
  (from `backEnd/basis/llm/cost.py`), and what effort, temperature and tokens mean.

Where the facts came from, verified rather than assumed:

- **Temperature** (`backEnd/basis/llm/providers.py` and `anthropic_provider.py`): no OpenAI
  gpt-5 or gpt-6 model and no Claude model is sent a temperature; they take the provider's
  default and cannot be set. Only the older non-reasoning models (`gpt-4.1-mini`,
  `gpt-4o-mini`) are sent 0. The live studies' call ledgers store temperature as null on every
  call, which agrees.
- **Effort**: each run's `run.json`, or the ledger of a live study; the earliest live runs (42.5
  runs 1 and 2) did not store it, and say "not recorded".
- **Tokens**: summed from each run's saved API usage (one row, 26.8's e2, re-added by hand from
  its 99 raw responses: 511,965 in / 99,681 out, 43,964 thinking, exactly as printed), from
  `run.json`, or from a live export's spend rollup. **Not recorded**: every per-photo run (15.1,
  28.1, the per-photo part of 26.2 and 26.8: their files keep the answer and the cost, no
  usage), every material second look and 16.2's overlap judgments (cost only), live run 2 (dollars
  only). (Corrected by the fact-check of 2026-11-03: 33.5's Haiku and Sonnet checkbox runs do have
  token counts in their records, now shown.) Those
  cells say so; nothing is estimated from cost. 15.1's 4c row also gives the tokens of the same
  setup run live on the same 52 photos (section 23, run 3). Section 32's load runs used fake
  providers and say so.

Corrections found on the way:

- 33.5's per-model cost: luna with the checkbox labels is $0.041 for 16 appraisals, 0.003 a
  document; the developer page had shown the grouped range's lower end, 0.002. The costs the page
